Tan‑Takneh can also deactivate one or both auto‑turrets remotely with a special command word.
datos.rutina:
(3 actions) With each action, the auto‑turret makes a longrifle Strike against a creature within 60 feet of Tan‑Takneh's campsite (other than Tan-Takneh). If there are no such creatures, the auto‑turret instead uses its action to sprout mechanical legs, totter 20 feet in the direction of its last target, and then plant itself into the ground again. Programmed to spread its fire around, the auto‑turret doesn't attack any creature it's already attacked in the round.

After making 15 Strikes, the auto‑turret depletes its ammunition and automatically deactivates.

burning-chandelier-trap.fuente: Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven
burning-chandelier-trap.descripcion: Four large flaming chandeliers swing wildly around the room.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 36 (master) to disable a chandelier or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 33) to permanently drain the magic from a chandelier. Any amount of cold damage that overcomes a chandelier's cold resistance extinguishes its flames and removes its persistent fire damage and flame dart attack. Thievery DC 41 (legendary) to disable the entire trap from the hidden control panel in the southeast corner of the room.
datos.rutina: (4 actions) For every chandelier disabled, the trap's actions are reduced by 1. For each of the trap's actions, a different chandelier attacks a random creature in the room. A chandelier uses its swinging chandelier attack if it can, but it can't make melee attacks against creatures in the cage, the closet, or the gap between the two double doors leading into the vault. Against a creature it can't reach with a melee attack, it uses a flame dart attack instead. The trap doesn't take multiple attack penalties.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets 1 minute after there are no living creatures remaining in the room.

captivating-gem.descripcion: The floating gem flares with inner radiance, sending out beams of light to captivate and drain the vitality from all who approach.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 35 (expert), Occultism DC 35 (expert), or Religion DC 35 (expert) to unravel the magical matrix within the gem, Crafting DC 40 or Thievery DC 40 check to unbalance the crystal's alignment, or a Athletics DC 43 check to damage one of the gem's facets and change its geometry; two successes are required to disable the hazard
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The captivating gem attempts uses all three of its actions to incapacitate creatures. It targets the closest creature with its Freezing Light ability, then a different creature with its facet flare Strike. If a creature has already been Paralyzed by Freezing Light, it chooses a different target for that ability.

clockwork-arms.fuente: Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale
clockwork-arms.descripcion: Four claw-tipped clockwork arms suspended from the ceiling pick up and deposit creatures into a nearby hatch.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to jam and deactivate one of the arms or Athletics DC 46 (legendary) to tear an arm off the machine.
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The trap loses 1 action per arm destroyed or disabled. On its turn, the trap makes claw Strikes against creatures other than the Rumormonger or the Inkmaster. If an arm already has a creature grabbed, the trap spends 2 actions to use its Open Hatch ability.

collapsing-bridge.descripcion: An iron bridge's connectors give way to drop into the lake below.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to disable one side of the bridge's quick release mechanisms

collapsing-structure.descripcion: Mogaru brushes against a structure, severely compromising the building's stability and possibly causing it to collapse.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 43 (master), Crafting DC 43 (master), or Engineering Lore (master) to brace the structure to reduce the risk of collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
datos.rutina: (1 action) The GM rolls a Flat DC 9 to determine if the building collapses, increasing the DC as listed above. On a successful check, dust and debris fall within the building and 30 feet around it, providing Concealment and dealing 6d6 bludgeoning damage to  randomly chosen targets (basic Reflex DC 35 save; on a critically failed save, the creature is knocked Prone). On a critical success, the effect is the same, but the debris deals 12d6 bludgeoning damage to  randomly chosen targets instead (DC 35 basic Reflex save; on a critically failed Reflex save, the creature is Restrained by rubble until freed , ]).
datos.reinicio: The building becomes susceptible to Shake Apart again {1d6 rounds} after it is stabilized.

collapsing-structure--pathfinder-lost-om.fuente: Pathfinder Lost Omens Monsters of Myth
collapsing-structure--pathfinder-lost-om.descripcion: Ebeshra brushes against a structure, possibly causing it to collapse.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 43 (master), Crafting DC 43 (master), or Engineering Lore (master) to brace the structure to reduce the risk of collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
datos.rutina: The GM rolls a Flat DC 9 to determine if the building partially collapses, increasing the DC as listed above. On a successful check, dust and debris fall within the building and 30 feet around it, providing concealment and dealing 6d6 bludgeoning damage to 1d4 randomly chosen targets (basic Reflex DC 35 save; on a critical failure, the creature is knocked Prone). On a critical success, the effect is the same, but the debris deals 12d6 bludgeoning damage to 2d4 randomly chosen targets instead (basic Reflex DC 35 save; on a critical failure, the creature is Restrained by rubble until freed , ]).
datos.reinicio: The building becomes susceptible to Shake Apart again {1d6 rounds} after it's stabilized.

deathly-dream.fuente: Pathfinder #173: Doorway to the Red Star
deathly-dream.descripcion: Sinister runes adorn the doorway, opening a portal to a realm of nightmares if anyone other than Dwandek opens the door.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to seal the rift using materials strongly grounded to the Material Plane, or Dispel Magic (7th‑level, counteract DC 33) to counteract the portal.
datos.reinicio: The deathly dream trap resets automatically as long as it hasn't been disabled or destroyed. Each time it resets, the tiny pocket plane of nightmare it sends its victim into resets as well, so no two victims will ever share the same deathly dream.

devouring-serpents.descripcion: Spectral serpents emerge from the ground to devour living creatures.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 38 (expert) or Religion (expert) to placate Yig, or Athletics DC 41 (master) to force the serpents' jaws closed; three successes total to disable the haunt
datos.rutina: The haunt makes a jaws Strike against each creature in the chamber as its first action. As its second action, it forces each creature hit by its jaws Strike to attempt a Reflex DC 34 save. On a failure, the creature is Grabbed until it {Escapes}. On a critical failure, or if the creature was already grabbed by the haunt, it becomes Restrained instead.

entropy-choir.fuente: Pathfinder #173: Doorway to the Red Star
entropy-choir.descripcion: A choir of ghostly shadows fill the benches in this room, chanting a haunting and unearthly melody.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 40 (master) to exorcise the spirits and break the power binding them into a single entity, or Performance DC 35 (expert) to counter the choir and nullify the destructive elements of its song
datos.rutina:
(3 actions; auditory, divine, evocation, sonic) The choir continues to sing its grim dirge every round until it is disabled or destroyed. If there are any non‑slowed living creatures in area A3 when its turn starts, it first uses Call to Nothingness as a single action.

It uses its remaining actions (or all three actions if there are slowed living creatures in the room already) to focus soul‑shattering choruses onto individual targets.

The choir can target any living creature in area A3 with an action, but never more than once per round per creature. It prefers to attack slowed creatures over all others, but it targets non‑slowed creatures if they're the only viable targets. A targeted creature must attempt a Fortitude DC 36 save.

—

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes 5d6 sonic damage.

Failure The target takes 10d6 sonic damage.

Critical Failure The target takes 15d6 sonic damage and increases their Drained condition by 1, to a maximum of drained 4.
datos.reinicio: The entropy choir resets automatically after 24 hours, even if it has been disabled or destroyed. It fades away forever once Dwandek and other members of the cult to which it sings its praises are destroyed.

eyeball-tank.fuente: Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale
eyeball-tank.descripcion: A vat of thick glass stands 10 feet high and is filled with green slime and fist-sized eyeballs.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 38 (master) or Crafting DC 34 (expert) to acidify the slime inside the tank, destroying the eyeballs
datos.rutina: (3 actions) Each round, the vat uses all three of its actions to shoot random eye rays at any living creatures (except Ixusoth) in range.
datos.reinicio: The trap can be reset by adding 100 new eyeballs to the tank and allowing them to grow in the slime for 1 week.

falling-stars-trap.descripcion: Pressure plates in the floor cause crystal‑tipped spikes to rain down into the room and explode.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to disable enough pressure plates so the trap won't trigger
datos.reinicio: The trap's supply of spikes magically replenishes, and the trap resets after 1 hour.

ghost-stampede.descripcion: Four massive skulls of aurochs, enormous wild cattle, rise into the air, each trailing its ghostly body behind it.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 36 (master) to calm one of the four aurochs or Religion DC 40 (trained) to exorcise them
datos.rutina: (4 actions) For each aurochs skull disabled or destroyed, the haunt has 1 fewer action. On each action, a different aurochs moves up to 60 feet and attempts a horn Strike against a different living creature. A creature critically hit by a horn Strike also takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage and is knocked Prone.
datos.reinicio: The haunt deactivates 1 minute after all living creatures leave the area or after all four aurochs skulls are destroyed. After 1 hour, if at least one aurochs skull remains, the haunt reactivates.

gorum-s-epitaph.descripcion: A section of ground thrusts up to form what looks like a mountain in which a sword has been impaled, and then the sword lashes out to stab at someone nearby. A successful DC 15 Religion check to  is enough to note that the hazard looks very similar to Gorum's religious symbol; any character who is at least expert in Religion notes this automatically.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to wipe away the faint runes scratched on the floor without activating a blade, or Religion DC 43 (master) to utter memorial prayers to Gorum to rob from the trap its violent energy
datos.rutina: (3 actions) If the Gorum's epitaph is adjacent to a creature, it uses its three actions to make greatsword Strikes on that creature (determining targets randomly if more than one creature is adjacent). Otherwise, it uses actions to Stride toward the closest visible target, then uses any remaining actions to Strike that target. Gray Master can flank with a Gorum's epitaph.

guardian-mural.descripcion: One of the carvings on the mural suddenly animates and clambers out of the painting to become a real creature in the middle of the chamber.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 35 (to deface the mural in precisely the right way to render it inoperable), or Dispel Magic (7th rank; counteract DC 34) to counteract the mural
datos.reinicio: 24 hours

mukradi-summoning-runes.descripcion: Barely visible runes are etched into the stone floor in a 20-foot diameter circle.

datos.desactivar: Acrobatics DC 36 to approach without triggering the trap followed by Occultism DC 34 (expert) or Thievery DC 38 (master) to erase the rune, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to counteract the rune.
datos.reinicio: The trap resets at the first high tide of each day.

nightmare-feast.descripcion: The consumption of sentient, and even sapient creatures is widespread in Leng. Those who suffer such fates are as much the genesis of this nightmare as those who partake, and as such, this nightmare tends to manifest in places where meals were taken, from banquet halls to campsites.

datos.desactivar: Society DC 43 (master) to fight these destructive urges by focusing your thoughts on traditions not so steeped in cruelty, or Intimidation DC 40 (legendary) to overwhelm the nightmare's influence with the strength of your own personality; three successes are required to disable the nightmare
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The nightmare transitions from directly chewing on the creatures in the area to compelling them to feed for themselves. Each round on the nightmare's turn, all creatures within 30 feet of the nightmare's epicenter must attempt a Will DC 36 save with the following results.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The nightmare causes a momentary change to the creature's appearance, causing its jaws to take on a frightening, fanged appearance and filling the creature's mind with distracting, unsettling hunger that cause them to become Off-Guard until the start of the nightmare feast's next turn.
Failure The creature becomes Confused until the start of the nightmare feast's next turn and gains a +30 bite (magical) that deals 3d12+10 slashing damage plus 2d6 persistent damage on a hit. The creature favors this bite Strike when the confusion drives them to attack.
Critical Failure As failure, but the creature also becomes Quickened and can use the extra action to make bite Strikes.
datos.reinicio: The nightmare deactivates as soon as a round begins with no creatures in its area, and resets in {1d6 rounds}.

pacification-ward.descripcion: A barely visible rune on the gate lock sprays nearby creatures with a soporific mist.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 36 (master) to block the rune's spray; or Dispel Magic (7th rank, counteract DC 34)

psychocybin-caps.descripcion: The mushrooms release spores that cause hallucinations, allowing the fungi to feed off the victim's psychic energy.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 35 or Survival DC 35 to cut back the mushrooms without triggering the spores
datos.reinicio: If a creature within 10 feet of psychocybin caps becomes Stunned 3, the effect generates enough mental energy to allow the fungi to reset.

rigged-ramen-cart.fuente: Pathfinder #173: Doorway to the Red Star
rigged-ramen-cart.descripcion: A seemingly innocent ramen cart is rigged to detonate if moved from its current location.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to disable the detonation trigger

rogue-sphere.descripcion: A roving sphere of distorted magic shimmers and floats through the air.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 38, Nature DC 38, Occultism DC 38, or Religion DC 38 (master) to cause the magic of the sphere to dissipate harmlessly, or Thievery DC 40 to cause the sphere to burst and implode safely, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34)
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The sphere uses its first action to fly 30 feet toward the closest creature currently under the effects of a spell, or it uses both actions to fly 60 feet toward the closest creature if none are within 30 feet. The rogue sphere attempts to enter the target's space. If a rogue sphere shares a creature's space, it uses an action to Magic Drift the target. If the target has no magical effects or carries no magic items, the result of its Fortitude save to resist the force damage caused by Magic Drift is increased by one degree of success.
datos.reinicio: The sphere ceases moving when no creature remains to trigger Magic Drift. It then dissipates after an hour spent with no targets within 60 feet

soul-pod.fuente: Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower
soul-pod.descripcion: An oblong, puffball-like fungus shaped ominously like a bulging coffin in which Aravashnial's distorted face can be seen silently screaming.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 40 three times to exorcise Aravashnial's soul from a pod, or Nature DC 43 twice to pull the well-hidden filaments that connect the spore pod to the rest of the spires
datos.rutina:
(2 actions) The soul pod releases a soulrending shriek on its first action, then on its second action exhales a blast of spore-laden wind in a 40-foot cone. Creatures in this area must attempt a Fortitude DC 36 save. This blast has the air and poison traits.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature takes 4d6 poison damage.
Failure The creature takes 8d6 poison damage and is knocked Prone by the wind.
Critical Failure The creature takes 16d6 poison damage, is knocked prone, and is blown 10 feet backward directly away from the soul pod, possibly being blown off the edge of a platform or stairwell.
datos.reinicio: A soul pod deactivates once no PCs are in the spires, then resets automatically.

window-alarm.descripcion: Transparent runes around the window's edge trigger a silent alarm shortly after being opened by an unauthorized person.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to carefully scuff the faint runes around the window's edge

acidic-needle-launcher.descripcion: A ceiling-mounted launcher rains resinous needles onto intruders, after which the needles melt into acid.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 36 to disable some firing mechanisms, making three adjacent squares in the trapped area safe to enter.
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The acidic needle launcher fires a needle at a random target in the area indicated on the map.

aethusa-s-prison.descripcion: A roiling sphere of chromatic energy floats above a pedestal marked with arcane symbols.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 42 (legendary) or Crafting DC 45 (master) to remove an immunity the prison currently has to one of the following damage types: acid, cold, electricity, or fire (this effect lasts until the prison uses its Energy Immunity reaction to regain that immunity); Arcana DC 42 (master) to fortify the pedestal's containment runes, preventing the prison from using its Chromatic Eruption action for 1 round and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts 20 untyped damage (this damage bypasses the prison's hardness and immunities); Thievery DC 42 (master) or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to suppress the pedestal's containment runes for 1 round, preventing the prison from using its Self-Repair action and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts 20 untyped damage (this damage bypasses the prison's hardness and immunities). Unlike most hazards, Aethusa's prison can't be disabled, but it can be destroyed by reducing it to 0 Hit Points.
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The prison uses its first action to Self-Repair. If the hazard has less than its maximum Hit Points, it then uses its Chromatic Eruption action.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and then resets automatically when it repairs to its maximum Hit Points.

cannibalistic-echoes.descripcion: A pack of cannibalistic spirits swarm through the area, devouring living creatures.

datos.desactivar: Intimidation DC 40 (master) to drive the spirits off with a ferocious display or Occultism DC 42 (expert) to exorcise the spirits
datos.reinicio: 1 day

collapsing-bridge--pathfinder-claws-of-t.descripcion: Metal supports twist and shear off the bridge, causing stretches of the structure to collapse.

datos.desactivar: Engineering-lore DC 40 to identify and reinforce weak points, Crafting DC 43 (master) to construct secondary supports, or Athletics DC 45 (legendary) to reinforce the bridge with found materials; three successes are required to halt the collapse
datos.rutina: (1 action) The collapse radiates out from the damaged section of the bridge. All squares adjacent to a collapsed section also fall into the water.

collapsing-vestibule.descripcion: A weak point in the barrier between the Universe and the Plane of Earth compromises the stability of the entire chamber.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 36 or Nature DC 36 (expert) twice to seal the rift between planes, or Stealth DC 34 to pass through the chamber without triggering the trap
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The hazard uses each of its actions to summon an elite Stone Mauler. Once the hazard has summoned a total of three stone maulers, it can’t summon another until the hazard resets. Alternatively, the hazard can use one of its actions to reassemble a mauler that has been reduced to 0 Hit Points. A reassembled stone mauler appears in the space it was destroyed with 100 Hit Points and is stunned 1. If the trap is disabled, any summoned stone maulers disappear as they return to the Plane of Earth.
datos.reinicio: Once all creatures have left the area, the hazard deactivates and the stone maulers disappear, but the hazard resets after 1 minute.

corrupt-grove.fuente: Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower
corrupt-grove.descripcion: A noisome mass of fungus at the center of the grove raises fungal guardians from the ground to defend itself.

datos.desactivar: Survival DC 42 (master) six times to carefully remove all the tangled fungal clots that absorb Tanglebriar's ambient energies for nourishment or Religion DC 45 (legendary) on the grove three times by a character who has holy sanctification and who uses prayer to exorcise the unholy energies that sustain the corrupt grove
datos.rutina: (1 action; poison, primal) The corrupt grove pulses and exudes a blast of toxic spores in a 60-foot cone that targets the area with the densest concentration of intruders. Creatures in this area take 8d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 37 save).
datos.reinicio: The corrupt grove resets 1 minute after no enemies are within the grove itself or attempting to damage the grove from beyond the crater's perimeter.

crushing-gate-trap.fuente: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
crushing-gate-trap.descripcion: A hidden stone rod causes two immense stone doors to fall forward from their gate, crushing anything beneath them. The doors also fall forward if touched.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 42 (expert) to secure the doors in place without triggering the trap

dread-aura.descripcion: The disturbing sensation of being watched, of having attracted the unwanted attention of something unimaginably powerful, or knowing the eerie conviction that unseen stars in the sky above might be looking down upon this spot grows increasingly overwhelming.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 45 (master) to inscribe eldritch warding sigils on the stones of the tower (this is an activity that takes 1 hour to perform) or defeat the Thresholder influence in the chambers below.

echoes-of-betrayal.fuente: Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City
echoes-of-betrayal.descripcion: Malevolent spirits led by a ghostly image of Ludika rise and begin a deadly brawl. These spirits attempt to overwhelm living creatures, forcing them to join the battle.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 35 (master) three times to exorcise the spirits or Diplomacy DC 39 (expert) three times to talk them down.
datos.rutina: (1 action) As 1 action, the haunt causes a barrage of ghostly fists to lash from the walls, floors, and ceiling. The haunt attempts a spectral fist Strike against each creature in area H10.
datos.reinicio: After 24 hours, the haunt returns. The spirits are permanently put to rest only if a lawfully appointed judge from Saggorak (or Kovlar) comes into the prison, takes damage from the haunt, and survives the attack.

flawed-memories.descripcion: The murky waters that fill the chamber grant false visions of the past.

datos.desactivar: Crafting DC 45 (master) to release alchemical reagents to neutralize the ink in the water, Nature DC 42 (legendary) to manipulate the primal magic in the region and negate the ink's effects, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to counteract the magical ink in the water; four success are required to disable it (spells that purify or manipulate water, such as Cleanse Cuisine or Control Water, can affect this hazard as if the caster were using an equal rank dispel magic)
datos.rutina:
(2 actions) On the trap's first action, it attempts a water jet ranged Strike on all creatures outside of the water in this room or on the stairs leading up to area A5. On its second action, the primal magic infusing the waters attempts to seep into the minds of those within it, forcing each creature in the water to attempt a Will DC 39 save against the following effects.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected
Success The creature takes 4d6 mental damage.
Failure The creature takes 8d6 mental damage and is Stupefied 2 for 24 hours. While the creature is stupefied, it takes an additional –2 status penalty to checks made to Recall Knowledge.
Critical Failure As failure, but 16d6 mental damage, Stupefied 3, and the stupefied condition has an unlimited duration.
datos.reinicio: The hazard remains disabled until Baolen refills the area with ink (typically once every 4 hours).

floating-flamethrower.descripcion: A floating skull of fire swoops around the arena, rotating as it weaves through the ring and releasing huge gouts of flame in random directions.

datos.desactivar: three Thievery DC 40 (legendary) checks or castings of Dispel Magic (7th rank; counteract DC 40), one each to pull out or disable the elemental cores hidden in the floating skull's right eye, left eye, and mouth
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The trap loses 1 action per turn per successful check to disable. The floating flamethrower uses its first action to release a gout of flame in a 15-foot cone that deals 4d6+4 fire damage (basic Reflex DC 40 save), its second action to fly in a U-shape in a random direction, and its third action to release another gout of flame.

freezing-floor-tiles.descripcion: Four remote sensors at each corner of the arena cause bursts of freezing magic to erupt from random tiles on the arena and stop creatures in their tracks.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (legendary) or Dispel Magic (6th rank; counteract DC 38) to disable one of the sensors
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The trap loses 1 action per disabled sensor. On each action, the trap causes a random 10-foot-by-10-foot space in the arena to suddenly freeze. Each creature that begins its turn in a frozen space takes 2d6+2 cold damage (basic Reflex DC 40 save). A creature that critically fails its save also becomes Slowed 1 for 1 round; if it was already slowed, the creature instead becomes Immobilized for 1 round. Any amount of fire damage dealt to a slowed or immobilized creature removes the condition. Frozen tiles become unfrozen at the beginning of the trap's next turn.

freezing-runes.descripcion: Spirals of cold energy rise from the runes to strike those sneaking food out of the area.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 36 (expert) to deactivate the runes, Thievery DC 38 (master) to scratch out the runes, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34)
datos.reinicio: Unless disabled or destroyed, the hazard resets automatically after being triggered.

lights-of-the-lost.descripcion: The murdered spirits of the slain priests manifest as churning, glowing spheres of floating, blood- red wine that drift and slither through the air. Within each can be glimpsed a silently screaming face.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 42 check to promise the restless spirits that justice will be served and the cause of their pain will be punished, or Religion DC 36 to invoke Cayden Cailean to calm the haunt.
datos.rutina:
(3 actions) Up to four different creatures in area A12 are each targeted by one of the floating, churning spheres of wine drifting through the air; it hurtles toward them and douses them with wine that turns to life- draining blood as it strikes unerringly. The haunt cannot target the same creature more than once each round. After the haunt is reduced to its broken threshold of 53 HP, it can target no more than two different creatures. A creature targeted by the lights of the lost must attempt a Fortitude DC 37 save.

—

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes 4d6 void damage and is Sickened 1 from drunkenness.

Failure The creature takes 8d6 void damage and is Sickened 2.

Critical Failure The takes 16d6 void damage, is Sickened 3, and becomes Doomed 1. As long as the creature is doomed from this trap, they cannot reduce their sickened condition below 1, and they take a -1 circumstance penalty on all further saving throws made against fear effects as lingering traces of the terror the priests felt loom in their memories.
datos.reinicio: 1 hour

mask-summoning-rune.descripcion: A cloud of invisible sensors in a 10-foot-radius surrounds an invisible floor rune.

datos.desactivar: Acrobatics DC 40 to approach a rune without triggering it followed by Thievery DC 42 (master) to erase the rune, or Dispel Magic (8th rank, counteract DC 34) to counteract the rune.
datos.reinicio: The trap resets each day at dawn.

memory-of-the-plateau.descripcion: An illusion of the Storval Plateau fills creatures with a longing for the surface.

datos.desactivar: Stealth DC 36 (master) to approach the crystal sphere followed by Thievery DC 38 (master) to remove the sphere from the pedestal without triggering the hazard, or Arcana DC 36 or Occultism DC 36 (expert) twice to unweave the illusion, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34)
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The hazard fills the hearts of those affected by the illusion with a longing for the surface. Each creature in the area that hasn't disbelieved the illusion attempts a Will DC 38 save. This is an emotion and mental effect.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature is Stupefied 1 for 1 round.
Failure The creature is Stupefied 2 and Slowed 1 for 1 round.
Critical Failure The creature is Stupefied 3 and Slowed 2 for 1 round.
datos.reinicio: The hazard deactivates automatically after 1 minute. The hazard reactivates after 1 hour unless the crystal is removed from the pedestal.

mirror-of-glory.fuente: Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star
mirror-of-glory.descripcion: A reflective field of energy fills a large archway in a gatehouse, in which viewers regard themselves dressed in fine clothes, bowing down before Runelord Xanderghul.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 37 (master) to disrupt one of the six anchor points that link the paradigm cube to the mirror, Arcana DC 34 (legendary) to use knowledge of magic that opposes pride to unravel the mirror's power, Intimidation DC 37 (master) to use one's force of personality to stand against the arrogance amplified by the mirror, or Dispel Magic (8th-rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract one of the six faces of the paradigm cube; six successes are required to disable the Mirror of Glory
datos.rutina:
(6 actions) On its turn, the Mirror of Glory targets random PCs in the area with distortions of their reality, spending an action to target one PC. If it has actions remaining after targeting the PCs, it spends any remaining actions repairing damage done to itself at the rate of 25 HP restored per action spent. If the mirror hasn't been damaged, then these unused actions are lost. Each time the Mirror of Glory targets a PC with a distortion, roll 1d6 and consult the entries below to determine what the PC experiences and any subsequent effects. The trap loses one action for each successful check made to disable it, but this doesn't reduce the number of distortions it's capable of creating. When a PC experiences a distortion, they take 10d6 mental damage (basic Will DC 37 save), but on a failed saving throw, the PC suffers that distortion's additional effect.
1—Beauty: The PC regards Xanderghul as the most attractive figure they've ever seen. Additional effect: Slowed 1 for 1 round.
2—Cruelty: The PC sees Xanderghul as a demonic figure capable of unimaginable cruelty, who lashes out at the PC with dozens of blades and poisoned needles meant to carve away their strength. Additional effect: Enfeebled 1 for 24 hours.
3—Disappointment: To the PC, Xanderghul suddenly seems to be an intimidating parental figure, commanding officer, or other person with authority whose disapproval induces tremors of nervousness. Additional effect: Clumsy 1 for 24 hours.
4—Jealousy: The PC watches as a glorious plume of peacock tail feathers spreads behind Xanderghul, filling them with jealousy and potentially driving them to lash out unpredictably against their allies in hopes of becoming the only one worthy of Xanderghul's attention. Additional effect: Confused for 1 round. 5—Despair: The PC feels their own flesh rotting away as they realize the Xanderghul who stands before them exists outside of the laws of time. Additional effect: Drained 1.
6—Worship: The PC is filled with the conviction that Xanderghul is the one true god and feels the urge to pray to him for absolution. Additional effect: Stunned 3.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates, then resets instantly.

nightmare-portal.descripcion: Horrific visions of a lumbering monstrosity whose face is nothing but a fanged mouth lurch out of the violet mist to attempt to eat the viewer alive.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 42 (master) to focus the portal's energies back in on itself to close it off, or Occultism DC 36 (master) to invoke the proper chant and make the proper hand gestures to untether the portal from the Dreamlands, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to counteract the portal for 1 minute and prevent Orgesh's influence from reaching through during that time
datos.rutina: (2 actions) A vision of an immense lumbering figure with nothing but a circular mouth for a face lurches out of the portal. For each action, the nightmare portal casts Phantasmal Killer (heightened to 8th level, Will DC 38), targeting a different creature both times. It can select targets in area E11, the secret alcove to the northeast, or up to 10 feet east from the door (although a closed door blocks it), choosing the closest two targets each round. The nightmare portal loses 1 action if it's broken and can thus only cast phantasmal killer once per round.
datos.reinicio: The nightmare portal resets 1 minute after it no longer detects targets.

nyrissa-s-tempest.descripcion: Sudden dark clouds gather in the sky above, and moments later, blasts of lightning and swirling tornadoes begin to rip the landscape apart.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 42 (master) to note the magical nature of the storm and to perform a quick ritual and prayer to the fey spirits of the region to cause the tempest to disperse, or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract the tempest immediately.
datos.rutina:
(4 actions) If the PCs successfully sought shelter with a Survival check, the storm takes no actions if the GM fails a Flat DC 16. Otherwise, the storm takes four of the following actions, each determined by rolling a , during the round. On each successive round, the number of actions the storm takes is reduced by 1; when the storm is reduced to 0 actions in this way, the hazard ends.

• 1 Thunderclap A blast of sound rips through the region. Unsheltered armies must attempt a DC 30 Morale check or increase their shaken value by 1. Unsheltered PCs take 10d6 sonic damage (basic Fortitude DC 38).

• 2 Lightning The tempest takes its Raging Storm reaction as a single action.

• 3 Tornado A tornado funnel extends down from the storm to unerringly strike at a PC, who must attempt a Fortitude DC 38 save.

—

Critical Success The PC escapes unscathed.

Success The PC is knocked Prone and takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage.

Failure The PC is hurled through the air, taking 8d6 bludgeoning damage and then falling 1d6×10 feet for appropriate falling damage, landing prone.

Critical Failure As failure, but 8d6 bludgeoning damage and a fall of 2d8 x 10 feet.

• 4 Renewal Blasts of wind tear through the area but do no real damage. Attempt a Flat DC 11; on a success, the number of actions the storm takes next round is not reduced as usual.

shadow-maze.descripcion: Shifting illusions disorient, entrap, and agonize those who attempt to pass through the shadowy maze.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 42 (master) to decouple faint strands of shadow essence from the magical matrix that holds the maze together, Arcana DC 45 or Occultism DC 45 to shunt the shadowy energy back into the Shadow Plane and render the maze inert, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 35) to counteract the shadow maze
datos.rutina:
(1 action; illusion, incapacitation, mental) The shadow maze shifts and adjusts its appearance, affecting all creatures currently located within its area. Any creatures in the area at this time must attempt a Will DC 37 save.

—

Critical Success The creature sees through the illusions and can act normally.

Success The creature treats all squares within the trap's area as difficult terrain, and the trap fills the creature's mind with sensations and false memories that it has been wandering these alleys for nearly an hour. The creature takes 5d6 mental damage from the perceived strain of navigating the alien flooded alleys.

Failure As success, but the creature believes it has been wandering the alleys for several hours. It becomes Slowed 2 for 1 round and takes 10d6 mental damage from the perceived strain.

Critical Failure The creature believes it has been hopelessly lost in the alleys of the shadow maze for days, and it is incapacitated for 1 round and takes 20d6 mental damage from the perceived strain.
datos.reinicio: If disarmed, the trap resets in 1 hour as long as the two crystals in area C5 still function.

spiral-seal.descripcion: A spiral shape suggesting the curling religious symbol of Pharasma is carved into the stone floor.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 37 (master) or Religion DC 40 (master) to unmake the Spiral Seal through occult ritual or prayer performed as a 10 minute activity with the Concentrate trait, or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 40) to counteract the Spiral Seal.

spiraling-comets.descripcion: Three blue comets orbiting the room turn red and attack when intruders enter.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 42 (master) to command each comet to disperse with Pharasmin prayers, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 42) to counteract each comet
datos.rutina: (3 action) The trap loses 1 action each turn for each comet disabled, counteracted, or destroyed. Each comet uses 1 action to attack the nearest intruder with a comet Strike.
datos.reinicio: The trap resets after 1 hour.

suffering-xulgaths.descripcion: The shadows of four xulgaths endlessly relive their deaths at the hands of the wendigos and their clutchmates.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 42 (master) or Occultism DC 42 (master) to calm each of the four spirits. On a character's first successful check, the character also learns that xulgath funerary rites typically involve cremation, which hints that fire is a viable way to put them to rest.
datos.rutina: (4 actions) Each active spirit chooses a living non-wendigo creature within 120 feet and attempts to devour it, targeting different creatures if possible. Each calmed spirit reduces the hazard's actions by 1
datos.reinicio: The haunt is deactivated and resets 1 minute after all non-wendigo creatures leave the area.

telepathic-whispers.descripcion: The spirits of the dead entice visitors with forbidden knowledge.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 40 or Religion DC 40 (expert) to ward off the spirits' influence, Intimidation DC 42 (trained) to silence the whispers. A PC who brandishes the gaze of eternity gains a +2 item bonus to their checks. Three successes total are required to disable the haunt.
datos.rutina: (1 action) The spirits peer into the minds of up to three creatures in the area. Each creature attempts a Will DC 40 save. On a failure, the target must choose to either divulge a closely guarded secret or take 4d8+18 mental damage. On a critical success, the target can ask the haunt a question, which the spirits answer truthfully to the best of their ability.
datos.reinicio: The hazard deactivates after 1 minute or after the spirits have answered three questions, whichever comes first. It resets after 24 hours.

waxworks-onslaught-trap.fuente: Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven
waxworks-onslaught-trap.descripcion: Four huge tubs containing congealed wax, enchanted to melt and envelop unwary intruders, each sit atop a cold fire.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to drain the wax from a tub or Athletics DC 45 (master) to push through the wax blocking a sealed door and escape (other creatures must push their own way through, as the wax reseals)
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The trap loses 1 action each turn per drained or destroyed tub. On each action, a different tub spews hot wax at a random creature in the room, dealing 3d12 fire damage to the target and all adjacent creatures (basic Reflex DC 35 save). On a failure or critical failure, the creature is also encased in hot wax. A creature that starts its turn encased in wax takes 8d12 fire damage and is Immobilized until it {Escapes} the hardening wax. Each turn it remains encased, the damage dealt by the hot wax decreases by 2d12 but the DC to Escape increases by 2 (minimum 0 damage, maximum DC 43). A creature that can't get free from the wax might suffocate.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 hour. At that time, the wax in the tubs cools and congeals, and any wax elsewhere in the room magically goes back into the tubs.

button-mash.descripcion: The room floods with harmful effects by pressing a magic sigil on a console. Each sigil causes different results. There are six sigils on the console.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 40 (master) to disenchant each sigil (can be done from either side of the reception desk), Thievery DC 43 (master) twice to disable the console (can only be done while behind the reception desk), or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 40) to counteract each sigil; prevent Noph from pressing the buttons by gaining access to the reception desk or other methods
datos.rutina:
(2 actions) Noph frantically pecks and stomps on the console, using each action to press a random sigil. Roll  to determine which sigil Noph presses. Psychopomps are immune to the effects of these sigils.

1 The area is flooded with holy light, dealing 3d12+19 vitality damage to each creature in the area (basic Reflex DC 43).

2 The area is flooded with unholy darkness, dealing 3d12+19 void damage to each creature in the area (basic Reflex DC 43).

3 The area is flooded with blue flames, dealing 3d10+19 fire damage to each creature in the area (basic Reflex DC 43). On a critical failure, a creature additionally takes 1d10 persistent damage.

4 A comet streaks through the area, attacking the nearest creature to Noph with a comet Strike.

5 Force tethers sprout from the floor, grasping at intruders. Each creature in the area is Immobilized for 1 round unless they succeed at a Fortitude DC 43 save.

6 Ghostly blue mist surrounds each psychopomp in the area, healing them 3d8+19 HP and granting them Concealment for 1 round.

caustic-vapor.descripcion: The door slams shut, and poison gas fills the room.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 36 (master) or Religion DC 36 (master) to exorcise the spirits
datos.reinicio: The trap resets after 1 day.

cleansing-fire.descripcion: Sheets of fire and vitality energy blast through the room in waves that obliterate the undead and scorch the living.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 41 (master) to bleed away the trap's energy, or Religion DC 39 (expert) to recite the appropriate prayers to Urgathoa to stop the trap (Pesabnet knows these prayers and automatically succeeds at checks to recite them). Disabling the trap requires three successful checks, in any combination of Thievery and Religion checks.
datos.rutina:
(1 action) A wall of sacred fire washes back and forth throughout the room, bathing every inch of the space in holy power and dealing 3d12 fire damage 3d12 vitality damage. Each creature in the trap's area must attempt a Reflex DC 39 save.

—

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes double damage.

Critical Failure If the creature has void healing, it is instantly destroyed. Otherwise, it takes double damage and 1d12 persistent damage.
datos.reinicio: The sacred fire disappears 1 minute after no creatures are in the room, and the trap immediately resets

diva-s-door.descripcion: A loud aria in a soaring tenor issues from the door, sending soundwaves outward.

datos.desactivar: Performance DC 38 (legendary) to cancel out the aria's soundwaves with another, Thievery DC 43 (master) to pick apart the arcane energies, or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract the trap

endless-elven-aging.descripcion: A haunted mural fascinates characters and swiftly drains their vitality.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 38 (master) or Religion DC 38 (master) to calm the restless energies and suppress the haunt for 1 hour; a critical success deactivates the haunt permanently.
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The haunt lures creatures into area A2 using Captivate. Any actions it hasn't used to Captivate are used to drain a living creature in the room with Live a Thousand Lives.
datos.reinicio: The haunt continues its routine until there are no targets within 30 feet of the room. It then resets over the course of 1 minute and is able to activate again.

guardian-guises.descripcion: Apparitions of Aroden in his various 12 guises (the shepherd, soldier, tailor, thief, and more) emerge in pairs to defend this room.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 43 (master), Intimidation DC 43 (master), or Religion DC 43 (expert); three successes are required to convince the trap that Aroden is truly dead, causing the Spiritual Guardians to hesitate and protest before fading away
datos.rutina: (2 actions; spirit) The hazard Sustains both spiritual guardians, either attacking or protecting at Kaisentia's direction. Once per round, if fewer than two spiritual guardians are present, the hazard conjures one new spiritual guardian from one of the statues as an action. Each statue can create only one spiritual guardian in this way before needing to be reset.
datos.reinicio: 1 day or after Kaisentia spends 10 minutes here in focused prayer

infernal-bow-shocks.descripcion: Wave after wave of Hellish power ripples out from the pentagram surrounding the Inferno Gate, bathing all of the battling armies around it in its dark energies. Some are slain on the spot, while others fall into cracks that open beneath them in the earth, and still others are consumed by ignited gasses.

datos.desactivar:
Devil Lore DC 34 or HellLore DC 34 to give the proper incantations and invoke the name of Visperthul to ward off the magical defenses from the Inferno Gate; Arcana DC 38 (expert), Nature DC 38 (expert), Occultism DC 38 (expert), or Religion DC 38 (expert) to erect a magical barrier to shield against the power emanating from the gate; Survival DC 43 to use the natural terrain as a shield to survive the onslaught of magical energies; Will DC 48 save to simply push back against the Hellish storm surge and refute them; or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 34) to blast the bow shock with magic to stem its flow; three successes are required to dissipate the hazard's energies.
The first time a PC successfully uses Devil Lore or Hell Lore against this hazard, all PCs gain a +2 status bonus to their saving throws against the hazard's effects.
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The infernal bow shocks release a different effect each round for 3 rounds, centered on a randomly-chosen PC each time and never the same PC twice in a row (though creatures standing near each other might just be unlucky). In the first round, it unleashes Flaming Fumes. In the second round, it uses an 8th-rank whispers of the void spell (DC 38), and in the third round, it emulates the effect of an earthquake spell (DC 38), with each of the three piles of tower rubble collapsing as though they were shoddy structures. Notably, no fissures extend into the former inner bailey of Fort Arego (area E4, as outlined by the remaining rectangular battlements). The hazard concludes for the PCs when it's disabled, or when the third round ends.

kharnas-s-lesser-glyph.fuente: Pathfinder #162: Ruins of the Radiant Siege
kharnas-s-lesser-glyph.descripcion: A hidden glyph suddenly lights up and dominates the mind of any creature not bearing the sigil of Kharnas the Angel-Binder.

datos.desactivar: Disable Thievery DC 46 (legendary) to destroy the glyph, Arcana DC 42 (master) to harmlessly divert the glyph's power, or Dispel Magic (7th rank; counteract DC 38) to counteract the glyph
datos.reinicio: The glyph can affect two creatures before it deactivates for 5 minutes and automatically resets.

planar-eviction-trap.fuente: Pathfinder Adventure: Night of the Gray Death
planar-eviction-trap.descripcion: An invisible magic rune emits a burst of psychic static and sends extraplanar creatures to Pharasma's realm.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 42 (master) or Thievery DC 42 (master) to discharge the glyph's power harmlessly, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 40) to counteract the glyph

rune-sentries.descripcion: Arcs of lightning arc flash from the eyes of the floating sentries.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 45 (legendary) to turn the lightning back against the sentry, causing the head to plummet, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the magic that empowers the sentry, causing it to plummet. Each sentry must be counteracted or destroyed separately.
datos.rutina: (6 actions) Each Rune Sentry grants the hazard 1 action; a Rune Sentry that's plummeted or been disabled or destroyed reduces the hazard's available actions by 1. On the hazard's turn, all active Rune Sentries spend their action to use Lightning Arc.

shrouded-assailant.descripcion: A spirit steps out of a covered mirror, pulling off and becoming shrouded in the cloth, which reveals the mirror. The shrouded figure attacks the living until the cloth is yanked off, which banishes the formless spirit.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to steal the cloth before the spirit manifests, or Athletics DC 47 to pull the cloth off the spirit after it manifests
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The spirit uses 3 actions to Step, fly 60 feet, or Strike, in any order. On a successful Strike the spirit's target is Frightened 1, and on a critical success, the target is Frightened 2.
datos.reinicio: The haunt is reset when the mirror is covered again.

sigil-of-deepest-fear.descripcion: An arcane sigil forces creatures to confront their greatest fear.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to drain the sigil's power harmlessly, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 42) to counteract the sigil
datos.reinicio: 1 day

sigil-of-deepest-fears.descripcion: An arcane sigil forces creatures to confront their greatest fear.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to drain the sigil's power harmlessly, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 42) to counteract the sigil
datos.reinicio: The trap resets after 1 day.

smoking-chimney.descripcion: Smoke billows out from the chimney and fills the room.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 40 (expert) to pull the blockage from the chimney, Thievery DC 46 (master) to clear the chimney by removing a crucial object and cause everything to fall out, or create water (or similar effect) to extinguish the fire
datos.rutina: (1 action; inhaled, poison) The smoking chimney billows out smoke. If the door from area A6 is open, the smoke expands 5 feet into the corridor. All creatures in the smoke take 11d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 43 save). On a failure, the target becomes Sickened 1 for 1 round.
datos.reinicio: The smoking chimney resets when 10 Bulk of objects are placed in it.

soul-stasis.descripcion: Four steel pillars emit pulsing energy to slow souls' processes.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 43 or Religion (master) to reweave the magic within each pillar, Thievery DC 46 (master) to disable each pillar, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 43) to counteract each pillar
datos.rutina: (4 actions) This trap loses 1 action each turn for each disabled pillar. Each pillar uses 1 action to emit a 30-foot-radius burst of inhibiting energy that slows souls. Each non-psychopomp creature with a soul in the area is Slowed 1 unless they succeed at a Fortitude DC 43 save.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any souls in the area.

spectral-opera.descripcion: A spectral cast of singers in opera costumes emerges from the walls, keening a mournful and terrifying chorus.

datos.desactivar: Performance DC 46 (master) to disrupt the song with another tune, or Religion DC 43 (expert) to calm the spirits

terror-glyphs.descripcion: Magical glyphs crawl across the floor, ceiling, and walls of the hallway.

datos.desactivar: Acrobatics DC 38 or Athletics DC 38 (expert) to move through the area before the glyph activates, Arcana DC 40 (expert) to unweave the glyph's animating magic, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36)

the-gullet.descripcion: Images of excessive feasts decorate the walls of the hallway.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (expert) to jam the hallway so it can't tilt; a character who succeeds at a Acrobatics DC 46 or Athletics DC 46 check can balance or sprint the length of the hallway before it has a chance to tilt. Flying creatures and Tiny creatures don't trigger the trap. Creative solutions (such as loading the hallway's western half with an appropriate counterweight) might also disable the trap.
datos.reinicio: Once the weight in the eastern end of the hallway is removed, the ramp rises back to its original position and the trap immediately resets.

the-trial-of-finality.descripcion: A shaft of light shines from the ceiling to the floor in a ring of slowly churning smoke.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to use tools to reflect and focus the light shining from above into the surrounding smoke to disperse it and the hazard's magical energies, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial
datos.rutina:
(1 or 2 actions; emotion, fear, mental) If a creature in area B4 is Paralyzed or Unconscious as a result of A Quick Death, the trial's first action is to Sustain that paralysis or unconscious effect; the paralyzed or unconscious creature can attempt a new Will DC 38 save at this time against this effect with the same potential results as detailed above for A Quick Death, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such save. The Trial of Finality's second action is to manifest horrifying ghostly shapes in the smoke that shriek and telepathically threaten everyone in area B4, promising them their deaths are imminent. All creatures other than the paralyzed or unconscious creature currently enduring A Quick Death must attempt a Will DC 38 save.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature becomes Frightened 1.
Failure The creature becomes Frightened 2.
Critical Failure The creature becomes Frightened 3 and is Fleeing as long as they remain frightened.
datos.reinicio: Once the room is empty of living creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

thisty-sands.descripcion: Illusory spectators cry out for blood as tendrils of sand hold unwilling combatants in place.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 38 or Nature DC 38 (master) twice to undo the magic that animates the sand, Intimidation DC 34 or Performance DC 34 (expert) twice to win over the crowd, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36)
datos.rutina: (1 action) Tendrils of sand rise from the floor. Up to two creatures in the room must attempt a Reflex DC 38 save. On a failed save, the tendrils wrap around the creature and move it to an unoccupied square closest to the center of the arena. If the creature was Flying, the tendril also pulls it to the ground. On a critical failure, the creature is also knocked Prone. The tendrils then collapse back into the floor.
datos.reinicio: The hazard deactivates once no living creatures are in the room, resetting after 1 minute.

trial-of-the-gods.descripcion: What appears to be an eye opens within the glowing orb near the ceiling.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to deactivate the glowing orb and prevent it from observing the room, Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial, Religion DC 45 (master) to perform a complex 5-round candle-lighting ritual, or placing General Ordulf's religious symbol on an empty hook on any wall as an Interact action
datos.rutina: (1 action; death, emotion, fear, mental) The red eye glances at a randomly determined creature in area B3 that it can see and is not engaged in a candle-lighting ritual, then casts a 9th-rank Vision of Death on that target, causing them to experience the sight of Achaekek rising up from the ground to smite the transgressor for failing to honor the gods.
datos.reinicio: Once the room is empty of creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

trial-of-tolerance.descripcion: A convincing illusion of a bustling market scene fills the empty room, confronting the viewers with potentially frightening diversity and unexpected encounters.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to scratch out well-hidden key runes etched into the room's floor, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the trial
datos.rutina: (1 action; emotion, fear, illusion, mental) An unexpectedly aggressive or frightening looking figure, such as a Hellknight, demon, pirate, or cloaked assassin suddenly emerges from the crowd and quickly advances toward a randomly determined character in the room, then stands menacingly in their path until the end of the round before they appear to lose interest and drift back into the crowd. If the target has a type of fear or hatred toward a specific kind of creature, this unexpected figure epitomizes those fears and hatreds. The target must succeed at a Will DC 46 save or become Frightened 1 (or Frightened 2 on a critical failure). If any creature in the room takes any hostile action against the intimidating figure, the Trial of Tolerance uses its Reflective Violence reaction. Once three rounds pass without the Trial of Tolerance using Reflective Violence, the hazard deactivates.
datos.reinicio: Once the room is empty of creatures, the trial deactivates and then resets after 1 minute has passed.

unspeakable-impressions.descripcion: A trail of over-sized footprints crosses the path, markings of the apparently recent passage of a dangerous and mind-shattering entity whose stride is enough to be mistaken for depressions in the natural terrain, and promising destruction to those compelled to follow the tracks.

datos.desactivar: Deception DC 46 (master) to distract those (including yourself) compelled to follow footprints, or Survival DC 43 (legendary) to quickly obscure the trail
datos.reinicio: The unspeakable impressions fade once they are triggered, but reform somewhere else in the vicinity 24 hours later unless they are successfully disabled.

wet-blanket.descripcion: Wet Blanket's invisible spirit plays a discordant tune that confounds the senses.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 40 or Intimidation DC 40 (expert) twice to convince Wet Blanket to stay silent, Occultism DC 42 or Religion DC 42 (master) to exorcise Wet Blanket's spirit, or Performance DC 38 (expert) twice to drown out Wet Blanket's music. A PC holding Wet Blanket's fiddle of the maestro gains a +2 item bonus to any check made to disable the haunt.
datos.rutina:
(1 action; auditory, concentrate, emotion, incapacitation, mental) Wet Blanket's tune causes creatures who hear it to act irrationally. Each creature in the area attempts a Will DC 40 save.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes immune to the tune for 1 minute.
Success The creature is Stunned 1.
Failure The creature is Confused for 1 minute. They can attempt a new save at the end of each of their turns to end the confusion.
Critical Failure As failure, and the creature immediately attacks themself. The Strike doesn't give the creature a flat check to recover from the confusion.
datos.reinicio: Unless the haunt is disabled, Wet Blanket falls silent once all creatures leave the room. She returns if another creature moves adjacent to the gate.

animated-mukradi-heads.descripcion: Three mukradi heads, animated by the souls of Zyphaniss's victims, rise into the air and fire energy throughout the room.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 40 or Religion DC 40 (expert) three times to cast out the souls animating the heads
datos.rutina: (3 actions) For each mukradi skull disabled or destroyed, the haunt has 1 fewer action. On each action, a different head moves up to 30 feet and attempts a maw Strike against a different living creature.
datos.reinicio: The hazard deactivates 1 minute after all living creatures leave the area or after all three heads are destroyed. After 1 hour, if at least one head remains, the hazard reactivates.

animated-parlor.descripcion: The items in the room, from the knick-knacks on the shelves to the logs burning in the fireplace, come to life and attack all creatures in the room.

datos.desactivar: Deception DC 44, Diplomacy DC 44, or Intimidation DC 44 (expert) to convince the items to stop attacking, Occultism DC 40 or Religion DC 40 (expert) to exorcise the soul fragments in the items; four total successes are required to disable the hazard
datos.rutina: (4 actions) On each action, the hazard makes an animated object Strike against a different creature in the room. For each successful check made to disable the hazard, the haunt has 1 fewer action.
datos.reinicio: The hazard resets 1 hour after it has been disabled. If destroyed, the hazard doesn't reset until Zyphaniss refurnishes the room, a project that takes several weeks.

ashes-of-despair.descripcion: Swirling ashes fill the room and form into the semblance of a massive predatory bird that swoops upon those in the chamber, draining their life force away.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 44 (master) to disrupt and counteract the shadow magic animating the ashes, or Religion DC 42 (master) to exorcise the animating spirit. Disabling the trap requires three successful checks, in any combination of Occultism and Religion checks.
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The shadowy shape sends streams of scouring ash toward the mouth, eyes, and nose of each creature in the room, dealing 3d12+20 slashing damage and requiring a Fortitude DC 42 save. Creatures that don't need breathe can't be sickened by the haunt and creatures that don't see can't be Blinded by it.

—

Critical Success The creature takes no damage and is blinded for 1 round.

Success The creature takes half damage, is blinded for 1 round, and is Sickened 1.

Failure The creature takes full damage, is blinded for 1 minute, and is Sickened 2.

Critical Failure The creature takes full damage, is blinded for 1 minute, is sickened 2, and is unable to use any spells or abilities with the verbal trait while it is sickened.
datos.reinicio: The haunt resets immediately when there are no creatures in area F9. Any previous successes from attempts to Disable the haunt persist when it's later triggered. After three successes, the haunt doesn't reset.

avian-rage.descripcion: Hundreds of panicked whippoorwills swarm through the area.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 43 (master) to calm the birds, Occultism DC 45 (master) to alter your aura, or Performance DC 45 (master) to imitate the living
datos.rutina: (1 action) The birds swarm wildly through the garden, pecking and slashing at all undead creatures and creatures with void healing in the garden, dealing 3d10+20 slashing,1d10 bleed damage (basic Reflex DC 44).
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any undead or creatures with void healing in the garden.

bittersweet-mask.descripcion: The many iron bars of this iron mask fits tightly around Javownir's head and snout, looking almost as if it was built in place to conform specifically to the shape of his skull with no apparent latch or hinge for it to be removed.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 45 (expert) twice to find the Hidden latches, Athletics DC 48 (master) to wrench the mask open quickly enough to prevent it from triggering before it's destroyed, Dispel Magic (9th-rank; counteract DC 35), or automatic with Spleen's key
datos.reinicio: The mask resets automatically at the start of the round after it is triggered.

carnivorous-mold.descripcion: Spores explode onto nearby creatures, leaving welts as the mold dissolves exposed flesh.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 42 (legendary) to neutralize the void energy that animates the mold, or Survival DC 36 (master) to remove the mold without triggering the spores

cataclysmic-planar-rift.descripcion:
This apocalypse represents the effects of numerous planar rifts forming and exploding in a region, with the risk of the planar fabric being compromised enough to tear a city-sized (if not larger) hole in reality. These rifts are likely to eject inhabitants of the other plane into the Universe, as well as serve as gateways for furious defenders to pour through to punish anyone they think might be responsible for the problem. Any additional encounters that result from these incursions should award XP as normal for encounters of their difficulty. While the rifts are likely to all lead to the same plane, particularly far-reaching disruptions might create gateways to multiple planes at once, with each rift spewing forth its own defenders. These groups would each have their own aims and agendas, clashing, collaborating, or causing chaos wherever they go.
Anticipate DC 40 Lore (expert) for the plane's Lore skill to notice pinpoint incursions from the other plane or Arcana DC 45 (master), Nature DC 45 (master), Occultism DC 45 (master), or Religion DC 45 (master) to detect subtle instabilities in the fabric of the Universe
Prepare DC 42 Lore (expert) with the plane's Lore skill, Arcana DC 45 (master), Nature DC 45 (master), Occultism DC 45 (master), Religion DC 45 (master) or Performance DC 48 (legendary) to perform a planar stabilization rite to minimize the damage

datos.rutina:
(1+ hours, Flat DC 18) Rifts detonate with raw planar essence. As the hazard progresses, the ruptures grow more frequent until they merge together into a gaping portal (this final stage might be prevented with good fortune or successful efforts to Prepare). Ruptures occur once per 10 minutes for the first hour and once per minute for the second hour. The frequency with which each unprepared creature in the area is hit by a rupture depends upon their proximity to the hazard's epicenter. If the hazard proceeds into a third hour, all creatures and objects in the area take the hazard's damage one final time before being swallowed up by the burgeoning portal and deposited on the other plane.
The planar explosions deal 2d12+18 damage, with a DC 42 basic saving throw, and inflict a condition on a failed saving throw. The damage type, saving throw type, condition, and condition duration depend upon the exploding plane, as detailed in the table below.
