cleansing-hall.descripcion: The hall's entry and exit seal with a force barrier, then waves of force surge through the hall.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 48 (master) to deface the script without triggering, Arcana DC 47 (master) to redirect the magical energy, or Religion DC 46 (master) to quote Pharasmin prayers
datos.rutina: (1 action) A wave of force flows down the hall from north to south, dealing 3d10+20 force damage to each creature in the corridor. Each creature must attempt a basic Reflex DC 40. On a failure, a creature is pushed back 5 feet (10 feet on a critical failure). If this movement would cause a creature to hit another creature, both creatures take 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If this movement would cause a creature to hit a force barrier, the creature takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage. Animals, plants, and worshippers of Pharasma are immune to this force damage.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.

cluster-heart.descripcion: A wave of magic passes through the area, causing crystal shards to grow and stab intruders.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 45 (master) to chip away at the crystal and disrupt its resonance, or Thievery DC 42 (master) to carefully detach the crystals and then safely smash them
datos.reinicio: Once the cluster heart uses its reaction, it automatically resets after 1 minute. As long as the cluster heart has 150 or more Hit Points, it recovers 50 per day.

collapsing-egorian-building.descripcion: Tremors from the changing landscape could cause a building to collapse.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 45 (master), Crafting DC 45 (master), or Engineering-lore DC 45 (master) to brace the structure against collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) decreases by 4 on a success (or by 8 on a critical success). Decreasing the flat check DC to 0 stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
datos.rutina: (1 action) The GM rolls a Flat DC 11, decreasing the DC as noted above. If the check fails, dust and debris fall within the building and 30 feet around it, providing concealment for 1 round and dealing 10d6 bludgeoning damage to 1d4 randomly chosen targets in the area (basic Reflex DC 40 save); a target that critically fails this save is also knocked Prone. If the flat check critically fails, the effect is the same, but damage from the debris increases to 16d6, it affects 2d4 randomly chosen targets, and a creature that critically fails its save is knocked prone and Restrained by the rubble (, ).
datos.reinicio: The building becomes susceptible to Shake to Pieces again {1d4 rounds} after it's stabilized.

covetous-corridor.descripcion: Statues depicting the runelords of envy steal magic from intruders.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 45 (master) to unweave the magic surrounding a statue, Athletics DC 48 (expert) to wrest a statue's implement from its hands, Thievery DC 48 (expert) to slip an implement free, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the magic that empowers the statue. Increase the DCs to disable the Belimarius statue by 2. Each statue must be disabled or counteracted separately, and disabling the Belimarius statue or all nine other statues permanently disables the hazard.
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The hazard uses Steal Magic twice. Once the implements of at least three runelord statues are charged, the hazard uses its next available action to Transfer Magic. If the hazard starts its turn with the Belimarius statue charged, the hazard uses its reaction to Empower Barrier. A disabled runelord statue can't use Steal Magic. If the Belimarius statue is disabled, the hazard can't use Transfer Magic or Empower Barrier.
datos.reinicio: The hazard resets automatically if not disabled.

crushing-threshold.descripcion: The ceilings of four alcoves slam down, threatening to crush everything inside.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) twice to Pick the Lock of the iron door or Athletics DC 44 (master) to  the door
datos.rutina: (1 action) The ceiling of one of the four alcoves—starting with the southernmost alcove and moving one alcove north each round—slams down with incredible force. A creature bracing the ceiling can prevent it from descending by making a successful Athletics DC 44 check, but the creature must repeat this check each round. The ceiling drops if the creature fails the check or leaves the alcove. Creatures and objects in an alcove when a ceiling drops each take 6d12+41 bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude DC 44 save). A creature that takes this damage also falls Prone. The contents of the alcove are then teleported to the secret hallway north of area H2, leaving the alcove filled with nothing but a block of solid stone.
datos.reinicio: Once the ceiling of the northernmost alcove descends, all four ceilings return to their original positions, the wall of force sealing the northern alcove disappears, and the hazard resets. Opening the iron door (even from the opposite side) permanently disables the hazard.

deadly-spinning-blade-pillar.descripcion: A spinning metal pole covered in deadly blades is hidden in the ceiling, connected to several trigger plates around the room and a hidden control panel built into the bed frame.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 39 (master) three times on a pillar, or Thievery DC 37 (master) twice on the control panel deactivates the whole trap. Breaking the control panel prevents anyone from disabling the trap using the control panel and prevents the trap from deactivating automatically (see Reset below)
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The trap uses its first action to make a spinning blade Strike against each adjacent creature. Its second action is to move in a random direction (roll 1d4 to determine the direction), and its third action to make a spinning blade Strike against each adjacent creature.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.

dragonstorm.descripcion: A massive storm stirs in the skies above Breachill and Citadel Altaerein. As specific events begin during the three waves of the manifestation's retribution, the dragonstorm wreaks localized havoc.

datos.desactivar: The dragonstorm can't be disabled-only endured. It ends only once the attack on Breachill and Citadel Altaerein is over.

false-prayer.descripcion: A statue dedicated to Ydersius fills the chamber with the divine glory of the Father of Serpents.

datos.desactivar: Deception DC 43 (master) to falsely proclaim the party's devotion to Ydersius, Religion DC 41 (master) to rededicate the statue to Yig, or Thievery DC 38 (expert) twice to pry the statue's eyes from their sockets
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The statue uses each of its two actions to cast a 9th-rank Blazing Bolt spell (DC 41), targeting up to three living creatures per casting. For each eye removed from the statue, the hazard has 1 fewer action. Until the beginning of the statue's next turn, the doors to area H17 don't require an Athletics check to Force Open (but opening them still requires an Interact action).
datos.reinicio: Unless the statue is destroyed, both its eyes are removed, or the statue is rededicated to Yig, the hazard deactivates and resets 1 minute after no living creatures are in the room.

flensing-floor.descripcion: Long saw-toothed blades slash up along the Hidden grooves in the floor, their edges caked with what looks like blood but is in fact a deadly poison.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 45 (master) once per weapon rack to detach the triggers from the trap mechanism
datos.rutina: (10 actions) The trap rolls a sawtooth saber Strike for each action, divided targets evenly among creatures in the trapped area. If there aren't enough targets in area B7 to divide these actions evenly, additional targets are randomly chosen. The trap loses one action for each destroyed blade. The trap ignores multiple attack penalties.
datos.reinicio: Manual.

flood-of-spirits.descripcion: A wave of spirits fly through the area, passing right through the living.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 48 (expert) or Religion DC 48 (master) to divert the spirits
datos.reinicio: 1 day

grasping-gauntlet.descripcion: A gauntlet of magical force clutches creatures trying to steal gear from the armory.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 45, Nature DC 45, Occultism DC 45, or Religion DC 45 to trick the hazard's magic into nullifying itself, Athletics DC 41 to wrestle the gauntlet into submission, Thievery DC 39 to slide an object into the gauntlet's grasp, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 41)
datos.reinicio: 1 hour

hardened-entry.descripcion: A portcullis drops from the ceiling, landing with a heavy thunk. Seconds later, a cloud of acid rises from a metal grate in the floor.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 45 to prevent the portcullis from dropping, Crafting DC 48 (master) to create a compound to neutralize the cloud of acid, or Thievery DC 35 (expert) to jam the pressure plate
datos.rutina: (1 action) A cloud of acidic vapor rises from the grate beneath the portcullis in a 5-foot emanation. Any creature that enters the area or starts its turn inside the cloud takes 3d12+20 acid damage (basic Fortitude DC 40 save). A creature that critically fails the save also takes 1d12 persistent damage. Each time the hazard uses this routine beyond the first, increase the radius of the emanation by 5 feet.
datos.reinicio: Once triggered, the trap must be manually reset by raising the portcullis. Once all the vials are smashed, the trap can't use its routine again until the vials are replaced.

hellfire-tornado.descripcion: The very air catches fire from the heat of a dragon's breath, causing a burning tornado.

datos.desactivar: The Hellfire tornado can't be disabled—only endured. It ends after 5 rounds.
datos.rutina:
(1 action; air, fire) The Hellfire tornado—a 15-footdiameter column 80 feet tall—moves 60 feet down the street. It can move through creatures' spaces, and creatures can move into its space, though the tornado's space is difficult terrain. Each creature the tornado moves through or each creature that ends its turn in the tornado's area takes 4d10 bludgeoning,4d6 fire damage (basic Reflex DC 40 save). A creature can be affected by the tornado only once per round.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature takes half damage.
Failure The creature takes full damage and rises 10 feet into the air as it's engulfed by the tornado (). While engulfed, a creature is Grabbed and Slowed 1, and if it doesn't have a fly Speed, it gains a 10-foot fly Speed until it either reaches the ground or ceases to be in the tornado's area, potentially falling when the hazard ends or when it leaves the tornado's area. A creature engulfed by the tornado moves along with it on the tornado's turn.
Critical Failure As failure, except the creature takes double damage and rises 20 feet into the air.
datos.reinicio: Once 5 rounds pass, the Hellfire tornado dissipates and doesn't reset.

host-of-spirits.fuente: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
host-of-spirits.descripcion: A host of angry spirits inhabiting the ruined house attempts to drag living creatures closer and crush them to death.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 43 (master) to exorcise the spirits or Deception DC 45 (master) to trick the spirits into departing
datos.rutina: 3 For each of its actions, the trap attempts a ghostly hand Strike against a different creature within 50 feet of the ruins of the house (if there are fewer than 3 creatures, the haunt doesn't use its remaining actions).
datos.reinicio: The haunt ends 1 round after no creatures are within 50 feet of the house. The haunt resets after 1 day.

ink-drowning-vats.fuente: Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale
ink-drowning-vats.descripcion: Steel hatch doors automatically lock shut in each of the four vats labeled J2. Four ink spouts (one per vat) jut through a narrow aperture in the ceiling of each vat, 20 feet above.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to seal an ink spout, Thievery DC 48 (master) to unlock a steel hatch door, or Athletics DC 45 (master) to Force Open a steel hatch door
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The trap loses 1 action for each disabled ink spout. On each of the trap's actions, a spout pours ink, increasing the depth of the ink in that vat by 2 feet. Creatures standing in the ink are exposed to a dose of poison ink. Once the vat is full of ink, the trap stops using actions, but creatures in the vat might start drowning.
datos.reinicio: The trap can be reset by refilling the ink storage tanks above the vats.

killing-fugue.descripcion: A vision of a terrifying presence (the King in Yellow, the Crawling Chaos, or some other horror beyond imagining) overwhelms an unfortunate explorer, putting them into waking stupor that quickly turns into a homicidal fugue.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 48 (master) to talk the affected individual out of the killing fugue, Occultism DC 45 (legendary) to recognize the spiritual attack taking place and help the victim to resist its effects; four successes are required to disable the nightmare
datos.rutina:
(3 actions; curse) The killing fugue attempts to force a creature under the stupefying effects of deathly vision into taking violent actions against their allies. The affected creature can still take its normal turn of actions on its own turn, but on the killing fugue's turn they perform actions as decided upon by the GM. The killing fugue then spends the appropriate amount of actions to perform those actions and activities. The affected creature can attempt a Will DC 40 save each time the killing fugue attempts to force them to take actions in this way with the following results.

—
Critical Success The character throws off the killing fugue's influence, ending the nightmare.
Success The character prevents the killing fugue from taking the attempted action or activity.
Failure The character is forced to take the action or activity chosen by the killing fugue.
Critical Failure As failure, but the character can no longer attempt Will saves to resist the killing fugue.
datos.reinicio: As long as a creature remains under the effects of the nightmare, it cannot reset. Once a creature has either recovered from the effects or died, the nightmare resets in {1d4 rounds}.

luminous-ward.descripcion: A burst of radiance explodes from the door.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to disable the wards or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 38) to counteract the ward
datos.reinicio: The trap resets after 1 hour.

maggot-pit.descripcion: Countless human-faced, fanged maggots wriggle and squirm in this chamber.

datos.desactivar: Three Religion DC 45 checks within the room to utter prayers, which calm and quell the maggots with invocations to the gods
datos.rutina: (2 actions; death, divine, necromancy) On its initiative, the pit uses its first action to use Damning Swarm against any creature within 5 feet of the pit floor. It then takes its second action to form a long, thrashing tendril composed of thousands of maggots to lash at a single target within area M1.
datos.reinicio: The pit functions continuously. If it's disabled or destroyed, it resets automatically after 24 hours if the crystal stele in area M2 still functions, otherwise it doesn't reset.

megatsunami.descripcion:
A tsunami can be a devastating disaster but pales in comparison to the daunting wall of water created by a megatsunami. When a megatsunami begins, ocean water often recedes far away from the shore, much more dramatically than it would during low tide. This warning sign might occur only seconds or minutes before the full force of the megatsunami crashes onto the land in the form of a wave whose height can exceed a hundred feet.
Anticipate Ocean-lore DC 36 (expert), Nature DC 38 (expert), or Survival DC 40 (master) to notice anomalies in wave patterns
Prepare Ocean-lore DC 36 (expert) or Nature DC 38 or Survival DC 38 (master) to chart the flood path, Crafting DC 38 (master) to reinforce a shelter, or Athletics DC 40 (expert) to quickly ferry people or supplies to higher ground

datos.rutina:
(5+ minutes, Flat DC 18) The megatsunami's wave overtakes and crushes everything in its path. It rips buildings off their foundations and tears up trees by their roots. Prepared creatures have managed to reach an area of high ground or another form of safety, but unprepared creatures in the area are caught up in the flood and battered by a combination of water and debris.
Unprepared creatures take 5d12+30 bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude DC 43 save) when the megatsunami hits and are thereafter surrounded by water. If they can't breathe water, they must hold their breath or begin to drown. Each round, a creature can attempt a Athletics DC 40 check to Swim up near the surface or to keep their head above water for the remainder of the minute once they reach the surface.
At the start of the next four minutes, the megatsunami has carried each unprepared character 250 feet inland. At this time, each unprepared character takes 3d12+20 bludgeoning damage (basic Reflex DC 40 save). A character who managed that minute to remain near the surface gains a result one degree of success better than their actual rolled result, with a critical success indicating they've managed to clamber out of the surge onto high ground and are now prepared.
At the end of the five minutes, attempt a Flat DC 18 to determine if a new wave repeats the routine. Characters already swept inland only become affected by these following waves once the rushing water reaches them, but until then they can Swim in the choppy floodwaters with a successful Athletics DC 30 check, potentially reaching safety or high ground before the next wave hits. Once a region is flooded by a megatsunami, it typically remains flooded for several hours.

orb-blast-trap.descripcion: Five globes shoot bolts of force up and down the hall when a second creature reaches its midpoint.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 48 (master) to deactivate the trap entirely before it triggers, Thievery DC 45 (expert) to deactivate one of the glimmering orbs after the trap rolls initiative, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 41) to deactivate the trap entirely.
datos.rutina: (5 actions) Five energized orbs each take one action to make a force bolt attack against a different target in the hallway (a single target cannot be fired at more than once per round by the trap). The trap doesn't take multiple attack penalties. Each orb that is disabled or destroyed reduces the trap's actions by 1.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates 1 round after it has no creatures to target and resets automatically after 1 minute.

phantom-soldiers.descripcion: Spirits of long-dead soldiers appear in the mist and attack intruders.

datos.desactivar: Intimidation DC 45 (legendary) to scare off the soldiers or Deception DC 46 (legendary) to order the soldiers to stand down
datos.reinicio: 1 hour.

revisit-past-pains.descripcion: A spirit locked in memories of its death flies down the hall, forcing intruders to experience the agony of its death.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 48 (master) to calm the spirit or Occultism DC 46 (master) to ward off the spirit
datos.reinicio: 1 hour.

shrieking-souls.descripcion: A terrified soul releases an earsplitting scream.

datos.desactivar: Diplomacy DC 44 (master) to comfort the spirit or Occultism DC 45 (master) to ward off the spirit
datos.reinicio: 1 hour.

slothful-stairs.descripcion: A supernatural exhaustion fills creatures who climb the stairs.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 45 (legendary) to wedge crumbling stones into cracks to jam the collapsing stairs, Thievery DC 48 (master) to deface the hidden magical runes that power the trap; or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract a rune; three total successes are required to disable the trap
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The haunt uses Leaden Limbs once, then Crumbling Stairs once.
datos.reinicio: The trap continues taking Leaden Limbs actions (and the void at the bottom of the stairwell remains open) for as long as creatures remain in the area. Once no creatures remain, the stairwell rebuilds itself, the void closes, and the trap resets.

smith-s-skull.descripcion: The smith's skull gazes with fiery light and breathes in a deep breath.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 48 (master) to hold the skull's jaw shut, or Occultism DC 45 or Religion DC 45 (expert) to quiet the Smith's spirit
datos.reinicio: 1 hour

stabbing-sentinel.fuente: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
stabbing-sentinel.descripcion: A petrified creature momentarily animates to attack an adjacent creature.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (master) to remove the animating magic without triggering the trap, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 38) to counteract the animating magic
datos.reinicio: The magical energy that animates the statue builds up again over 24 hours and the trap resets.

storm-discharge.fuente: Pathfinder Lost Omens Monsters of Myth
storm-discharge.descripcion: Ebeshra aligns its crystalline form to produce a blast of lightning that charges the surrounding area with electrical energy.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 45 (master) to balance the electrical charges in the area or Deception DC 48 (expert) to momentarily divert Ebeshra's attention
datos.reinicio: Ebeshra waits  rounds before another blast.

swatting-tail.descripcion: Mogaru's tail sweeps forth, causing an arc of devastation in a 60-foot cone.

datos.desactivar: Performance DC 45 (legendary) or Deception DC 48 (legendary) to momentarily divert Mogaru's attention
datos.reinicio: Mogaru doesn't swat his tail again for {1d4 rounds}.

trinity-star.descripcion: A blazing comet with three tails—one red, one black, and one with rainbow hues—careens throughout the area.

datos.desactivar: Athletics DC 48 (legendary) to grab one of the comet's tails and rip it free; Occultism DC 45 or Religion DC 45 (master) to exorcise the divine energy of the red tail (which is infused with Gorum's legacy) or the black tail (infused with the nihilism of Abaddon's Eclipse); Arcana DC 45 (master) to unweave the magic of the rainbow tail (Xanderghul's mythic power); or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract one of the tails. Each tail must be disabled separately to disable the hazard.
datos.reinicio:
(1 action) The Trinity Star flies at a speed of 60 feet, moving through the spaces of as many creatures as possible. Each creature the Trinity Star moves through must make a Reflex DC 42 save with the following results.

—
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.
Success The creature takes 6d6 force damage.
Failure The creature takes 11d6 force damage and is knocked Prone.
Critical Failure The creature takes 22d6 force damage, is knocked prone, and if the creature is mythic, they lose 1 Mythic Point. If the Trinity Star has lost any of its tails, it regrows one of them (chosen at random if it's lost two tails).

venom-pool.descripcion: A shallow, foul-smelling puddle of toxic acid blocks a narrow hall (marked with a dotted line on the map), and poison bursts from it when disturbed.

datos.desactivar: Crafting DC 40 (master) or Survival DC 42 (legendary) to neutralize the acid while within reach of it. Three successes using either skill (or a combination of both) destroys the hazard.
datos.rutina: (2 actions) The hazard uses its first action to spread 10 feet down the hallway in both directions. Once out of the hall, each side spreads in a random direction each round, but they don't go through doors. The hazard uses its second action to move the center of the Toxic Cloud up to 20 feet in any direction to which any part of the pool has line of effect (normally, to encompass the greatest number of characters). If the cloudkill isn't present, it instead uses its second action to produce a new cloudkill, as Poison Puff.
datos.reinicio: The hazard ends after 1 minute, contracting to its original size and keeping still until disturbed again.

void-bars.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
void-bars.descripcion: Bars made of pure Void energy block access to the far side of the cell.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 45 (master) three times to deface the well-hidden focusing runes etched along the walls, or Dispel Magic (10th rank; counteract DC 38) to counteract the void bars
datos.rutina: (1 action) Each set of void bars manifests a long arm made of darkness that reaches out and attempts to Strike a creature in the room, favoring targets that previously damaged the bars or attempted to disable them, but otherwise choosing a target randomly from those available. This void talon can extend to attack any creature in the room or within 20 feet of the cell door in the outer hall, but targets in the outer hall gain the benefit of cover against this attack.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates at the end of a round in which no living creatures are in the cell, then immediately resets at the start of the next round.

witch-priests-curse.fuente: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
witch-priests-curse.descripcion: Anyone who opens a secret compartment is subjected to a powerful curse.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 39 (legendary) to carefully remove the bone fetish that holds the curse.
datos.reinicio: The trap resets if both secret compartments are shut.

zutha-s-legacy.descripcion: The scowling visage of Runelord Zutha appears above the altar. Meanwhile, mask-like versions of Zutha's face manifest on nearby rubble and vomit swarms of maggots. Once the masks are destroyed, the air fills with spectral duplicates of Zutha's life-draining bone scythe.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 45 (legendary) or Religion (legendary) to exorcise Zutha's spirit, or Intimidation DC 48 (master) or Performance DC 48 (master) to recite the details of Zutha's defeat; six total successes are required to disable the haunt.
datos.rutina: (4 actions) The haunt uses Vomit Maggot three times, then Poisonous Belch once. For each success at Disabling the haunt, the haunt loses one Vomit Maggot action. Destroying a mask also removes one of the haunt's Vomit Maggot actions. Once the haunt can no longer use Vomit Maggot, it immediately regains three actions and replaces Vomit Maggot with Spectral Scythe. Destroying a scythe also removes one of the haunt's Spectral Scythe actions. Once the haunt loses all three of its Spectral Scythe actions, the haunt is destroyed.
datos.reinicio: The haunt deactivates once no living creatures remain nearby. The haunt resets 1 hour later.

apocalypse-stormfront.descripcion: An endless void stretches in all directions. Visions of Golarion's destruction roll like storm clouds across the space.

datos.desactivar: Acrobatics DC 47 to Fly through the space without becoming stuck in the webs, Athletics DC 50 to Climb the webs and make progress forward through the infinite, Nature DC 47 or Occultism DC 47 or Arcana DC 50 or Religion DC 50 (legendary) to collapse the extradimensional space, or Perception DC 52 to peer through the visions of Golarion to notice discrepancies that help keep the overwhelming despair from setting in; six successes disables the hazard, causing it to vanish forever and shunting all creatures to Liralarue's Prison.
datos.rutina:
(1 action) (arcane, emotion, illusion, mental) A stormfront filled with illusory scenes of Golarion's destruction rolls through the extradimensional space. Each creature in the hazard's area takes 6d12 mental damage (basic Will DC 42 save). On a failed save, a creature is also Doomed 1 (Doomed 2 on a critical failure). A PC reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is shunted back into area C7.
A creature that takes damage while Climbing the webs must succeed at a Fortitude DC 40 save or fall. A creature can try to Grab an Edge (Reflex DC 40). On a success, they lose one success they've earned to escape the hazard but otherwise arrest their fall. On a failure, they plummet into the void, losing all Athletics successes they've earned to escape the hazard. Each round on their turn, the character can try to Grab an Edge again, but each time they fail to do so, the party must earn an additional success to escape the hazard. Characters who fall Unconscious or repeatedly fail to Grab an Edge might effectively become lost in the void, though once the nightmare hazard is disabled, they appear along with the rest of the PCs in Liralarue's Prison.
datos.reinicio: The hazard resets automatically once no creatures are in the area.

blackfinger-s-prayer.fuente: Pathfinder #162: Ruins of the Radiant Siege
blackfinger-s-prayer.descripcion: The trapdoor's metal is infused with a deadly toxin that seeps out when the trap is triggered.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 50 (legendary) to gum up the trapdoor's porous metal surface, Crafting DC 45 (master) to render the toxin inert, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 45) to counteract the trap's magic

castigate-the-faithless.descripcion: Magic forces those who pass by the statue to the ground with sudden force; pressing the bypass button deactivates the trap for 1 minute.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 47 (legendary) to deactivate the trap through prayer, Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 47) to counteract the trap, or press the bypass button
datos.reinicio: The trap resets automatically if triggered, after 1 minute if the bypass button is pressed, or after 15 minutes if disabled or counteracted.

cleansing-suite.descripcion: Deadbolts inside the doors clunk as three glowing runes appear on the ceiling.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 42, Nature DC 42, Occultism DC 42, or Religion DC 42 to erase the runes, or Crafting DC 46 or Thievery DC 46 to destroy the runes, or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 41); each rune requires a success to remove (three runes total)
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The cleansing suite activates one of its runes. The hazard can't activate the same rune more than once per turn. Disabling a rune removes one of the hazard's actions and prevents the hazard from activating that rune.
datos.reinicio: 1 minute after the hazard activates, the deadbolts unlock and the hazard resets.

damurdiel-s-vengeance.descripcion: An elven woman wearing a robe stands in the water. She beckons anyone who enters the room to join her in the pool.

datos.desactivar: Deception DC 45 (legendary) to pretend to be Erveniss and ask for forgiveness, Diplomacy DC 45 (legendary) to convince Damurdiel to stand down (elves who are masters in Diplomacy can attempt the check as if they were legendary instead), or Religion DC 40 (legendary) to call upon Calistria to calm Damurdiel's spirit.
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The haunt attempts to Strike with the dagger.
datos.reinicio: Damurdiel's spirit subsides once she is destroyed or if she manages to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points. She returns after 1 minute.

dimensional-darkside-mirror.descripcion:
A magic mirror replaces characters with evil mirror duplicates from another dimension.
The mirror can't be damaged while any mirror duplicate is alive

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 40 (legendary) to retrieve a creature from the other dimension within 10 minutes of the switch (possible only if their mirror duplicate is dead), Thievery DC 45 (master) to permanently disable the mirror once all mirror duplicates are dead, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 37) to counteract the mirror for 1 minute and prevent additional replacements during that time
datos.rutina: (1 action) The mirror absorbs another reflected creature into the mirror and replaces it with a mirror duplicate. Mirror duplicates attack on their own initiative, using the same statistics as the original creature, but with an evil alignment (changing only abilities that shift with the alignment change). A mirror duplicate can spend 3 actions in contact with the mirror to return to its original dimension and release the creature it duplicated, but most mirror duplicates prefer not to.
datos.reinicio: The mirror is always ready to absorb creatures into the other dimension. Ten minutes after a creature is sucked into the mirror, if an ally doesn't rescue the creature with Thievery, it reaches the other dimension, where it might be captured or killed. In the mirror dimension, it counts as a mirror duplicate, so the denizens of the other dimension can't destroy the mirror on their side while the absorbed creature is there. These dimensions are alternate realities, not planes, so even rituals like plane shift can't reach them.

distortion-circle.descripcion: A softly flickering circle of runes pulses and periodically distorts the air above it before a raw red wound in reality splits open to disgorge demons and lash out with tendrils of acidic blood.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 47 to erase key runes from the circle, defeat all four summoned demons in combat, or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 36)
datos.rutina: (1 action) On its initiative, the trap extends a tongue-like appendage covered with sharp teeth. The tongue snaps like a whip, firing a volley of sharp teeth at a non-demon target in the room. The trap can precisely sense the location of all viable targets in the room, and teeth fired from the tongue penetrate the many wooden shelves (although a character with at least one shelf between it and the trap gains greater cover).
datos.reinicio: The distortion circle deactivates (and any summoned demons vanish) at the end of any round in which no viable targets for the tongue to attack are in area C10. The trap then immediately resets (and is ready to summon a new batch of four demons).

electrified-gate.descripcion: A warded metal gate electrocutes anyone who touches the gate without pressing the bypass button.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 47 (legendary) to destroy the ward, Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 47) to counteract the ward, or press the bypass button
datos.reinicio: The trap resets automatically if triggered, after 1 minute if the bypass button is pressed, or after 15 minutes if disabled or counteracted.

fang-fungus-cage.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
fang-fungus-cage.descripcion: A mass of hundreds of long thin fang-shaped fungal growths protruding from the wall encase and pierce the flesh of an elven prisoner.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 41 three times to delicately cut the elf free without causing the fungus to react, or Medicine DC 47 two times to gently manipulate the fungus loose from where it's tendrils have penetrated flesh, or Athletics DC 50 to swiftly wrench the elf free from the cage before the fungus can react
datos.reinicio: A fang fungus cage resets instantly.

fungal-colony.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
fungal-colony.descripcion: A ring of dead trees covered in dry fungus suddenly shakes and rattles as if something inside some of the trees were about to explode.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 45 twice to appeal to spirits of the natural world still lingering in the area and ask them to neutralize the infestation, Survival DC 39 four times to gently break open four key tree trunks in the colony to allow the spores to vent harmlessly, or Thievery DC 48 to trigger a chain reaction among the logs that forces the hazard to implode dramatically but harmlessly. Once the hazard is triggered, only the Nature check can disable it.
datos.rutina:
(1 action; poison, primal) The 120-foot-tall plume of spores turn toxic. Each round, the spore cloud's highest point drops by 40 feet, and it expands outward from the initial perimeter at A2 by 20 feet on the ground and at a height of 10 feet. At the end of the third round, the spore cloud stabilizes as a ten-foot-high ring with a width of 45 feet, which completely fills the clearing with ease. This spore cloud doesn't obscure vision, but creatures that end their turn in it take 5d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 41 save).
On round 4, the spore cloud settles to the ground on the hazard's action. If the hazard hasn't yet been disabled, the ground between areas A1 and A2 erupts, and a trio of fungus-encrusted warsworns, their bodies composed of ancient elven skeletons bound together by glistening filaments of mold, rises up to attack all intruders in the area. At this point, the hazard deactivates, but the warsworns fight until they're destroyed.
datos.reinicio: 24 hours after the fungal colonies erupt, the hazard reactivates and can trigger again. If the warsworns are activated and destroyed, they do not appear again on a subsequent triggering.

fungal-engine.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
fungal-engine.descripcion: A thick mass of pulsing fungi and mold infested with ghostly shapes cakes the walls of the room.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 41 seven times to seek out and remove seven specific nodes of fungi that govern the intake and dispersal of energy, or Religion DC 47 three times to exorcise the souls out of the engine and force it to shut down
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The fungal engine expels clouds of toxic spores on its turn, causing all non-fungi and non-demon creatures in the room to take 10d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 41 save); any creature that takes damage is exposed to grayshroud.

—
Grayshroud
Saving Throw Fortitude DC 40
Stage 1 Fatigued (1 day)
Stage 2 Drained 1 and fatigued (1 day)
Stage 3 Drained 2 and fatigued (1 day)
Stage 4 Drained 3, fatigued, and can't speak (1 day)
Stage 5 death
datos.reinicio: The fungal engine deactivates and resets after 1 minute, but any demons called in remain in the area for an hour to ensure the intruders don't return.

fungal-forge.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight

datos.reinicio: A fungal forge resets immediately at the start of every round, and immediately triggers again if there are still sapient creatures within it.

guthallath-rockslide.descripcion: The rock walls nearby begin to crumble and collapse.

datos.desactivar: Crafting DC 48 (legendary) to buttress the collapsing rocks in three different locations. Using large and durable materials (or applicable spells) to support the rocks reduces the check to Crafting DC 45 (master).
datos.rutina:
(2 actions) On the hazard's first action, any areas of crumbling rocks from a previous round collapse, making a falling rocks Strike against each creature in the area.

On its second action, the hazard crumbles rocks in a 20-foot radius around the previous collapse. A character can Seek (DC 40) to determine where the rocks will fall on the following round, but on a critical failure, they incorrectly identify where the rocks will fall.
datos.reinicio: The guthallath can reset the hazard with a few days of work stacking the fallen rocks.

imperious-darkside-mirror.fuente: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
imperious-darkside-mirror.descripcion: This magic mirror replaces characters with evil duplicates from another dimension.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 42 (legendary) to retrieve a creature from the mirror within 10 minutes of the switch (possible only if their mirror duplicate is dead), Thievery DC 47 (master) to permanently disable the mirror once all mirror duplicates are dead, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 40) to counteract the mirror for 1 minute and prevent additional replacements from appearing during that time.
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The mirror absorbs another reflected creature into the mirror (Reflex DC 42) and replaces it with a mirror duplicate. Mirror duplicates act on their own initiative, using the same statistics as the original creature, but with an evil alignment (changing only abilities that shift with the alignment change).

Mirror duplicates are legendary in Intimidation and are permanently Quickened, but they can use this additional action only to Demoralize.

A mirror duplicate can spend 3 actions in contact with the mirror to return to its original dimension and release the creature it duplicated, but most mirror duplicates prefer not to.
datos.reinicio: The mirror is always ready to absorb creatures into another dimension. 10 minutes after a creature is sucked into the mirror, if an ally doesn't rescue the creature using the Thievery skill, the creature reaches the mirror dimension, where it could be captured or killed. In the mirror dimension, it counts as a mirror duplicate, so the denizens of the other dimension can't destroy the mirror on their side while the absorbed creature is there. These dimensions are alternate realities, not planes, so even rituals like Interplanar Teleport can't reach them.

living-paints.fuente: Pathfinder #162: Ruins of the Radiant Siege
living-paints.descripcion: A mass of brushes use magical paint to convert creatures into art.

datos.desactivar: Crafting DC 41 (master) to mix the paints into bland, useless colors, Thievery DC 41 (legendary) to dismantle the animated brushes, or Dispel Magic (8th rank; counteract DC 41) to counteract the magic within the paint.

mental-scream-trap.descripcion: A psychic scream disorients creatures in the area.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 41 to suppress the magic or Thievery DC 41 to scratch out the ward

meteor-shower.descripcion:
Impact from a sufficiently large asteroid would be powerful enough to wipe out a region or destroy a planet, but smaller-scale impact events, like from a meteor shower, present hazards that could be survived. This shower might arise naturally, or it might be the result of the PCs or other forces preventing a greater calamity by breaking a world-rending asteroid into smaller pieces.
Anticipate Astronomy-lore DC 41 (master) or Nature DC 45 (legendary) to notice signs of the approach of unusual celestial bodies
Prepare Astronomy-lore DC 40 (master) or Nature DC 50 (legendary) to predict the trajectory of the falling asteroids and determine safe zones, Athletics DC 45 (legendary) or Crafting DC 47 (master) to dig underground shelters, Diplomacy DC 45 (master) or Intimidation DC 47 (master) to coordinate an orderly evacuation

datos.rutina: (1+ minutes, Flat DC 17) Small asteroids rain down across the sky, battering and incinerating those caught in their path before carving craters. Over the course of a minute, enough asteroids smash into the ground and explode to inflict 6d10 bludgeoning,14d6 fire damage to any unprepared characters in the area (basic Reflex DC 44 save). The 40-foot-radius craters left behind are greater difficult terrain.

paranoia-well.descripcion: Sudden invasive emotions of fear, paranoia, and anger well up in the mind, causing companions to take on sinister casts to their no-longer familiar features.

datos.desactivar: Intimidation DC 47 (legendary) to shout down the emotional energies and exert mental dominance over them, or Thievery DC 44 (master) to cause the trap's energies to discharge harmlessly

praise-of-yog-sothoth.descripcion: Magical letters reveal phrases in Aklo that, if not properly spoken aloud, inflict numbing cold.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 47 (master) or Religion DC 49 (master) three times in a row to successfully speak aloud the esoteric phrases as they appear (this causes the trap to deactivate for 1 hour, although the phrases continue to appear during this time), or Dispel Magic (9th rank, counteract DC 38).
datos.rutina: (1 action) The trap fills the entirety of area B4 with additional blasts of cold. All creatures in area B4 take 12d6 cold damage (basic Fortitude DC 41, plus Immobilized for 1 minute on a critical failure).
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates 1 round after it has no target creatures and resets after 1 minute.

rift-portal-network.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
rift-portal-network.descripcion: A six-foot-tall green mushroom with red spots on its cap is connected to seven rifts in surrounding alcoves by tendrils of vapor.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 50 once to delicately cut out or destroy the seven points on the mushroom that connect to the rifts, Religion DC 41 seven times (once per rift) to exorcise the demonic influence, or Planar Seal (10th rank, counteract DC 39) to counteract the planar link in this room
datos.rutina: (7 actions) Each round, each of the seven rifts fires a beam of demonic energy into the room, targeting one creature (regardless of alliance to Tanglebriar) at random. A single creature cannot be targeted by more than one rift beam per round, so if there are fewer than seven potential targets, the rift portal network loses any remaining actions for that round.
datos.reinicio: The network deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any creature moving in area D4 and without any attempt to disable it.

seismic-spears-trap.descripcion: Lines of searing lava lance through the area, causing targets to shake as if caught in an earthquake and potentially become petrified.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 43 (master) to disable the wards or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 38) to counteract the ward.
datos.reinicio: The trap resets after 1 minute.

siphoning-spirit.descripcion: A formless spirit drains life from the living, becoming progressively visible as its victims weaken.

datos.desactivar: Occultism DC 48 (expert) or Religion DC 48 (expert) to weaken the spirit; four total successes are required to disable the haunt
datos.rutina:
(1 action; death, divine, necromancy, void) The spirit inhales, siphoning the souls of the living and becoming more visible. Each creature within 60 feet takes 4d10+20 void damage, with a Fortitude DC 41 save. If no creatures are within the area, the haunt moves up to 120 feet into the largest concentration of living creatures and then inhales.

—

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and increases its Drained value by 1, to a maximum of drained 4.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and increases its drained value by 2, to a maximum of drained 4. If the creature was already drained 4, it dies.
datos.reinicio: After 1 minute, the spirit is satiated, and the haunt deactivates as it returns to a resting state. Over the course of 1 hour, the spirit's siphoned life energy disperses and the haunt resets.

skewering-hall.descripcion: A dozen spears hidden within sockets in the walls thrust into the hall when the pressure plate is triggered.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 47 (master) to disable the pressure plate

skinclock.descripcion: Blood sprays from clock's straight razor hands, forming a large set of oversized blood red razors that slice out to hew at flesh and bone.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 47 once on the clock's hands and once on its face to decouple both of the magical sensors in the trap from each other, or Dispel Magic (10th rank, counteract DC 39) to counteract the trap
datos.reinicio: The Skinclock resets automatically.

soul-drinking-spirit-collectors.descripcion: Four spirit collectors drain the souls from nearby creatures.

datos.desactivar: Religion DC 47 (legendary) to sever the connection between Urgathoa and each spirit collector, Thievery DC 50 (legendary) to deactivate each spirit collector, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 50) to counteract each spirit collector
datos.rutina: (4 actions) This trap loses 1 action each turn for each disabled spirit collector. Each spirit collector uses 1 action to drain the souls of all creatures within 30 feet, dealing 4d10+20 force damage (basic Fortitude DC 46). On a failed save, a creature becomes Drained 1 and Stupefied 1 or increases their drained and stupefied conditions by 1 (by 2 on a critical failure).

supervolcanic-eruption.descripcion:
Volcanic eruptions are dramatic events in which magma erupts from a planet's mantle onto its surface. They're often preceded by earthquakes and the opening of fissures in the ground that vent toxic gases. These initial signs can occur months or even years in advance, making it difficult to predict the eruption's timing. While the intensity, features, and progression of eruptions vary, this hazard represents the most dangerous variety of eruption, one that can swiftly overtake cities with rapid tides of superheated gas and rock and spew out enough ash to affect the climate for years. When these sorts of eruptions are also supervolcanos, eruptions with the highest degree of explosive force, they cause unparalleled transformation to the landscape and alter climate on a planetary scale.
If you're looking for something more supernatural, it's a relatively simple change to adjust the energy damage caused by a supervolcano's pyroclastic flow to something else—for example, a cloud of ghosts erupting from a long-lost city might inflict mental, spirit, or void damage instead of the fire or electricity damage a normal pyroclastic flow brings. Just be sure to give the new event a suitable description that matches the new type of damage!
Anticipate Mountain-lore DC 40 (master), Survival DC 42 (master), or Nature DC 45 (legendary) to predict the eruption's arrival
Prepare Mountain-lore DC 42 (master), Survival DC 45 (master), or Nature DC 48 (legendary) to determine evacuation paths, Medicine DC 45 (master) to safely treat and relocate people poisoned by toxic gases in the preceding days, Athletics DC 48 (master) to relocate people and essential supplies, or Crafting DC 48 (legendary) to create filtration systems and barricades capable of withstanding a pyroclastic flow

datos.rutina:
(24 hours) When the hazard begins, toxic gas vents open throughout the affected region, followed by clouds of ash. As the eruption column collapses, material rushes forth from the volcano in a pyroclastic flow, which is followed by a dense ash cloud that persists for several minutes. Ash and toxic gas persist for up to 24 hours.
Ash limits visibility like a thick fog, deals 2d6 fire damage per minute, and creates difficult terrain as it collects on the ground. The ash also generates bolts of ash lightning. Once per minute, one unprepared PC takes 3d12 electricity damage (basic Fortitude DC 46 save). Pockets of dense ash are particularly dangerous. Unprepared creatures in areas of dense ash must hold their breath or begin to suffocate.
When the pyroclastic flow first hits a region, creatures in its path must attempt a Reflex DC 43 save with the following results (prepared creatures increase their roll by one degree of success).

—
Critical Success The creature avoids most of the pyroclastic flow, but still takes 3d6 fire damage and treats all movement in the area as greater difficult terrain for the next 10 minutes.
Success The creature takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage and 3d6 fire damage, and is buried in ash and debris. While buried, they can't breathe and take 4d6 fire damage each round at the start of their turn until they succeed at a DC 40 check to Escape, in addition to the normal 1d6 bludgeoning damage each minute for being buried.
Failure As success, but 6d6 bludgeoning damage and 6d6 fire damage, and .
Critical Failure As success, but 12d6 bludgeoning damage and 12d6 fire damage, and .

teleport-trap.descripcion: The House at the Edge of Time folds time and space back on the target, who teleports painfully into their own body an instant before they travel.

datos.desactivar: This trap cannot be disabled as long as Nyrissa lives, but if she is slain or forgiven, the teleport trap vanishes.

the-avalanche.fuente: Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds
the-avalanche.descripcion: The Avalanche rests as a gem on a stone pedestal, continually unleashing natural disasters in the nearby area.

datos.desactivar: Two Athletics DC 41 or Survival DC 43 checks to approach the pedestal, resisting the quaking earth and other hazards and eventually holding strong enough to take the gem from the pedestal; a creature who can approach the pedestal without touching the ground, such as by jumping or flying, can simply snatch the gem and end the Avalanche's assault
datos.rutina:
(1 action) The Avalanche releases its fury at a point within 120 feet, affecting all creatures within its area. Each creature must attempt a Reflex DC 41 save to hold their ground or avoid the incoming danger. The amount and type of damage dealt are based on the nature of the natural disaster the Avalanche unleashes, and certain types of disasters impose additional effects. The Avalanche can't unleash the same type of disaster twice in a row. The sturzstromer is immune to these effects.

Earthquake The ground in a 20-foot burst violently shakes and launches rubble in the area, dealing 3d12+20 bludgeoning damage. On a failure, the creature also stumbles back 5 feet, away from the Avalanche. On a critical failure, the creature stumbles back 10 feet and is knocked Prone.

Fire Rain A hail of burning rock rains down in a 20-foot burst, dealing 3d12+20 fire damage. Creatures that fail their save catch on fire and take 2d6 persistent damage (double on a critical failure).

Landslide A mass of rubble falls in a 20-foot burst, dealing 9d8 bludgeoning damage. Creatures that critically fail their save become trapped under this rubble as if it were an avalanche, except a creature can attempt to Escape from beneath the rubble (DC 40).

Lava Channel A burst of molten rock violently spews forth in a 30‑foot‑long and 10‑foot‑wide line, dealing 9d8 fire damage. Creatures that fail their Reflex save are swept 15 feet away by the lava (30 feet on a critical failure). The lava cools almost instantly, allowing creatures to walk over its path immediately after resolving the effects of the disaster.

Powerful Winds A massive burst of wind travels in a 60-foot line, kicking up dust and dealing 3d12+20 slashing damage. Creatures that fail their Reflex save become Dazzled for 1 round and also fall prone on a critical failure.

—

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage.

the-eclipse.fuente: Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds
the-eclipse.descripcion: The Eclipse is located high in the sky, manifesting as an eclipsed sun.

datos.desactivar: Reduce the Eclipse to 0 HP, or Dispel Magic (10th rank; counteract DC 39) to counteract the Eclipse (once it's in range)
datos.rutina: (1 action) The Eclipse heals 50 healing points of damage, retreats upward from PCs if any have approached (as determined by its Distance Score), then unleashes a meteor down on the island below. The meteor explodes upon striking the island, creating a 30-foot burst that inflicts 8d6 fire damage and 4d6 bludgeoning damage (basic Reflex DC 41 save) to all creatures caught in the blast. The eclipse targets these strikes to catch as many PCs in the blast as it can each time—while it doesn't seek to damage a bul‑gae, it won't worry about catching one or both in the area of effect if that spot is the most advantageous to striking the most possible PCs.

the-winder.fuente: Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale
the-winder.descripcion: A large metallic arm, 20 feet long, is set into the floor. It rotates around the room to wind up nearby clockwork creatures.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 50 (master) to deactivate the system, or Athletics DC 40 (legendary) to jam the gears for 1 round
datos.rutina: (1, 2, or 4 actions, depending on the encounter's threat level) The Winder uses each of its actions to Wind clockwork assassins in the room, starting with inactive ones.
datos.reinicio: The Winder resets as soon as no creatures remain in the room.

witchbole-s-heart.fuente: Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight
witchbole-s-heart.descripcion: A sphere of tangled branches and roots, encrusted with fungus and mold, suddenly animates and reaches out several claw-like limbs.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 50 to exorcise the corrupted spirit trapped within the Witchbole's Heart, or Thievery DC 47 three times to deactivate the Hidden runes scribed in the sphere that allow the corrupted spirit to animate limbs (each one of these successful Thievery checks reduce the hazard's routine by 1 action)
datos.rutina: (3 actions) The Witchbole's Heart forms several long, thin, spiky limbs tipped with poisonous talons. On each of its actions, it attempts to Strike one non-demon creature in reach of the central sphere. The Witchbole's Heart does can't attempt to Strike a single target more than once per round.
datos.reinicio: The Witchbole's Heart deactivates and resets automatically 1 minute after no targets remain.

zyphaniss-s-soul-cage.descripcion: The malevolent spirit inside the soul cage defends itself against attempts to remove it from the avatar's forehead.

datos.desactivar: Arcana DC 48, Nature DC 48, Occultism DC 48, or Religion DC 48 (legendary) three times to break the entropic vaultline's magical connection to the avatar. Once the connection is broken, the soul cage loses its Hardness, and its AC is reduced to 40. Destroying the soul cage disables the hazard. Alternatively, three successful Thievery DC 45 (legendary) checks remove the soul cage from its socket, disabling the hazard but leaving the soul cage intact. Reducing the avatar of Yig to 0 HP also disables the hazard.
datos.rutina:
(1 action) If the avatar of Yig's Annihilation Beams are available to use, the hazard focuses both beams in a 20-foot burst within 120 feet. The ground in the area becomes difficult terrain. Any creatures in the area take 15d10 untyped damage (no damage type) and must attempt a basic Reflex DC 43 save with the following effects. A creature reduced to 0 HP is reduced to a fine powder as the Disintegrate spell. The hazard can't use this action again until the avatar's Annihilation Beams become usable again.

—
Critical Success The creature takes no damage.
Success The creature takes half damage.
Failure The creature takes full damage and is knocked Prone.
Critical Failure The creature takes full damage, is knocked prone, and is Stunned 1.
datos.reinicio: If the avatar of Yig hasn't been reduced to 0 Hit Points and Zyphaniss's soul cage is removed from it without being destroyed, the avatar reactivates with full HP as soon as the soul cage is returned to the socket on its forehead.

angry-vegetation.descripcion: Five large flowers in the weed-choked field unfurl, each dusting pollen onto vines that animate into Wemmuths.

datos.desactivar: Nature DC 48 (master) or Performance DC 48 (legendary) to calm a flower, closing it
datos.rutina:
2 If there are fewer wemmuths than open flowers, the flowers create more wemmuths (so there as many wemmuths as open flowers) as their first action.
For their second action, the flowers produce a mind-addling pollen. Each non-plant creature within 30 feet of a flower must succeed at a Fortitude DC 41 save or become Slowed 1 for 1 round (or Confused for 1 round, on a critical failure). The pollen is an emotion, mental, and olfactory effect.
datos.reinicio: Wemmuths collapse into ordinary vines and the trap resets if the area is left alone for 1 minute.

animated-cage-trap.descripcion: A spiky iron cage pulls in a victim with animated chains before slamming shut and locking tight.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 45 (master) to Pick the Lock, Athletics DC 48 (master) to break the lock or bend the bars; five total successes are required to disable the trap
datos.rutina: (3 actions) As 1 action, the trap makes a chain Strike against a target in its reach; its Athletics modifier for Improved Grab is +36. The trap can have any number of creatures Grabbed or Restrained by its chains. If the trap has any creatures grabbed or restrained, it attempts to pull them closer as 1 action with an Athletics check against the creature's Fortitude DC; on a success, it pulls the creature 5 feet closer (10 feet on a critical success). A Large or smaller creature can be pulled inside the cage, after which the cage door slams shut. The cage can only contain one creature, and that creature is restrained while inside (). As 1 action, the trap can Constrict the creature inside the cage with more chains.
datos.reinicio: The trap deactivates 1 minute after there are no longer any potential prisoners in the room and then activates 1 round after that.

axiomatic-polymorph-trap.descripcion: A Utopian glyph transforms trespassers into aeons.

datos.desactivar: Thievery DC 48 (master) to drain the glyph's power harmlessly, or Dispel Magic (9th rank; counteract DC 42) to counteract the glyph
datos.reinicio: 1 hour

cataclysmic-planar-rift-escalation.descripcion:
This apocalypse represents the effects of numerous planar rifts forming and exploding in a region, with the risk of the planar fabric being compromised enough to tear a city-sized (if not larger) hole in reality. These rifts are likely to eject inhabitants of the other plane into the Universe, as well as serve as gateways for furious defenders to pour through to punish anyone they think might be responsible for the problem. Any additional encounters that result from these incursions should award XP as normal for encounters of their difficulty. While the rifts are likely to all lead to the same plane, particularly far-reaching disruptions might create gateways to multiple planes at once, with each rift spewing forth its own defenders. These groups would each have their own aims and agendas, clashing, collaborating, or causing chaos wherever they go.
Anticipate DC 43 Lore (expert) for the plane's Lore skill to notice pinpoint incursions from the other plane or Arcana DC 48 (master), Nature DC 48 (master), Occultism DC 48 (master), or Religion DC 48 (master) to detect subtle instabilities in the fabric of the Universe
Prepare DC 45 Lore (expert) with the plane's Lore skill, Arcana DC 48 (master), Nature DC 48 (master), Occultism DC 48 (master), Religion DC 48 (master) or Performance DC 51 (legendary) to perform a planar stabilization rite to minimize the damage

datos.rutina:
(1+ hours, Flat DC 18) Rifts detonate with raw planar essence. As the hazard progresses, the ruptures grow more frequent until they merge together into a gaping portal (this final stage might be prevented with good fortune or successful efforts to Prepare). Ruptures occur once per 10 minutes for the first hour and once per minute for the second hour. The frequency with which each unprepared creature in the area is hit by a rupture depends upon their proximity to the hazard's epicenter. If the hazard proceeds into a third hour, all creatures and objects in the area take the hazard's damage one final time before being swallowed up by the burgeoning portal and deposited on the other plane.
